Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Baqarah (The Cow) because it uniquely mentions the story of the cow which God commanded the Children of Israel to slaughter. This cow had a divine role in exposing the crime of murder committed by some of the Children of Israel, who had colluded to conceal the identity of the killer.

Some of the Surah's Objectives

• Extolling the status of the Qur'an, and dividing people, in terms of their benefit from its guidance, into four categories: believers, polytheists, hypocrites, and People of the Book.

• Exhorting and commanding taqwa (God-consciousness), describing the attributes of the muttaqun (the God-conscious), and calling believers to adhere to God's laws and not transgress within them, through stories, promise and warning.

• Mentioning the beginning of the creation of man, and bestowing favour upon people by the preference of their forefather, Adam (peace be upon him), over the creatures of this world, and how the enmity of Satan towards Adam and his descendants arose, in preparation of the hearers' souls to be alert to the whispering of Satan.

• Discourse about the Children of Israel, reminding them of God's blessings upon them, and their response to those blessings by deviating from the straight path, explaining a number of their characteristics, and recounting some of their social and religious circumstances.

• Explaining the virtues of the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the excellence of Abraham (Ibrahim), who built it, and that the religion of Islam is founded upon his creed (millah), which is monotheism (tawhid).

• Arguing with the polytheists using the signs of God's creation, recounting their state on the Day of Resurrection, refuting their claims of prohibiting what God has permitted to them, and mentioning a category of polytheists who concealed enmity towards Islam while displaying affection for the Muslims.

• Explaining a number of legislative rulings related to the affairs of the Islamic state, the family, and transactions, such as jihad, retaliation (qisas), fasting, pilgrimage (hajj), oaths, some financial transactions, charity, the prohibition of wine (khamr) and gambling (maysir), marriage, the system of marital living, some rulings concerning women, and other matters.

• Explaining the creed of the believers and the distinctive features of the Islamic Shari'ah, and directing the believers to repentance and humble supplication to God, to lift from us obligations that are burdensome to us, and to grant us victory over the disbelievers.

[Tafsir]

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ These letters, and other disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs, contain an indication of the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an. By it the polytheists were challenged, and they were unable to produce its equal, though it is composed of these very letters from which the Arabic language is formed. The inability of the Arabs to produce the like of it, despite their being the most eloquent of people, proves that the Qur'an is a revelation from God.

That is the Qur'an, the Great Book about which there is no doubt that it is from Allah. It is not correct for anyone to doubt it, because of its clarity. It benefits the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) with beneficial knowledge and righteous action; they are those who fear Allah and follow His rulings.

They are those who believe in the unseen, which their senses and their intellects alone cannot perceive, since it is known only through the revelation of God to His messengers, such as belief in the angels, Paradise, and Hellfire, and other matters that God or His Messenger (ﷺ) has informed us of. Faith (al-iman) is a comprehensive term for affirming belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both its good and its bad; and the affirmation of faith is confirmed by speech and action, by the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. Along with their belief in the unseen, they maintain the prayer at its prescribed times, performing it correctly in accordance with what God prescribed for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and they spend from what We have provided them, giving in charity from their wealth, both the obligatory and the recommended.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 4:

Those who believe in what has been sent down to you, O Messenger, of the Qur'an, and in what has been sent down to you of wisdom (al-hikmah), which is the Sunnah, and in all that was sent down before you to the messengers in scriptures, such as the Torah and the Gospel and others, and they believe in the abode of life after death and what it contains of reckoning and recompense, belief that is in their hearts and becomes evident on their tongues and their limbs. The Last Day was singled out for mention because belief in it is among the greatest incentives to performing acts of obedience, avoiding what is forbidden, and holding oneself accountable.

Those who possess these attributes are upon light from their Lord and by the guidance of their Creator and Guide, and they are the successful ones who have attained what they sought and been saved from the evil from which they fled.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 7:

Allah has sealed the hearts of these people and their hearing, and has placed a covering over their sight, because of their disbelief and obstinacy after the truth had become clear to them. So He did not grant them success in being guided, and for them is a severe punishment in the Fire of Hell.

And among the people are those who waver, bewildered between the believers and the disbelievers: they are the hypocrites (munafiqun) who say with their tongues, "We believe in God and the Last Day," while in their inner selves they are liars who have not believed.

They believe, in their ignorance, that they are deceiving Allah and those who believe, by displaying faith while concealing disbelief. But they deceive only themselves, for the consequence of their deception returns upon them. And because of the extent of their ignorance, they do not perceive this, due to the corruption of their hearts.

In their hearts is doubt and corruption, so they were afflicted with sins that bring about their punishment; so Allah increased them in doubt, and for them is a painful punishment, because of their lying and hypocrisy.

When they are advised to stop spreading corruption on the earth through disbelief and sins, and by disclosing the secrets of the believers and allying themselves with the disbelievers, they say, falsely and argumentatively: "We are only people of reform."

This is the commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 12, from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar. Here is the translation of the passage:

Indeed, what they do, and what they claim to be reform, is in fact corruption itself; but because of their ignorance and obstinacy, they do not perceive it.

When it is said to the hypocrites, "Believe, as the Companions believe," which is faith with the heart, the tongue and the limbs, they argue and say, "Shall we believe as the feeble-minded and the foolish believe, so that we and they are equal in foolishness?" Allah answers them by saying that foolishness is confined to them, while they do not know that what they are upon is misguidance and loss.

These hypocrites (munafiqun), when they meet the believers, say: "We affirm Islam just as you do." But when they depart and go back to their leaders, the disbelievers who rebel against Allah, they assure them that they have not abandoned the creed of disbelief. They were only making light of the believers and mocking them.
Allah mocks them and gives them respite, so that they increase in misguidance, bewilderment and vacillation, and He will requite them for their mockery of the believers.
Those hypocrites have sold their souls in a losing bargain: they took disbelief and abandoned faith, so they gained nothing; rather, they lost guidance. And this is the clear loss.

The condition of the hypocrites who professed faith—outwardly, not inwardly—in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), and then disbelieved, so that they came to stumble about in the darkness of their misguidance while not perceiving it, with no hope of emerging from it, is like the condition of a group in a dark night. One of them kindled a great fire for warmth and light; but when the fire blazed and illuminated what was around them, it went out and left them in darkness, so its people were in utter blackness, seeing nothing, unable to find a path or a way out.

They are deaf to hearing the truth with reflective hearing, mute in speaking it, and blind to seeing the light of guidance. Therefore they cannot return to the faith they abandoned, and they have taken misguidance in its place.

Or the condition of another group of hypocrites is like that of people walking in the open, where a heavy rain pours down on them, accompanied by darkness layered upon darkness, along with the crashing of thunder, the flashing of lightning, and destructive thunderbolts, which, from the intensity of their terror, make them put their fingers into their ears for fear of death. And Allah is all-encompassing over the disbelievers; they cannot escape Him, nor can they overpower Him.

The lightning nearly snatches away their sight, due to its intense flashing. Yet whenever it lights up for them, they walk in its light, and when it departs, the way grows dark upon them, so they stand still in their places. Had God not granted them respite, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight, and He is able to do that at every moment. Indeed, God is over all things competent.

A call from God to all of mankind: worship God, who has nurtured you with His blessings, fear Him, and do not oppose His religion; for He created you from non-existence, and created those before you, so that you may be among the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) whom God is pleased with and who are pleased with Him.

Your Lord is the One who made the earth a spread-out bed for you, so that your life upon it would be made easy, and the heaven a well-built structure; and who sent down rain from the clouds and brought forth thereby fruits of various kinds and plants of every sort as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to God in worship, while you yourselves know that He alone creates and provides, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped.

And if you are in doubt, you disbelieving obstinate ones, about the Qur'an which We have sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ), and you claim that it is not from Allah, then produce a surah like a surah of the Qur'an, and call upon whomever you can of your helpers besides Allah, if you are truthful in your claim.

If you fail to do so now, and you will certainly fail in the future, then guard yourselves against the Fire by believing in the Prophet (ﷺ) and obeying God, the Exalted. This is the Fire whose fuel is people and stones; it has been prepared for those who disbelieve in God and His messengers.

Say, O Messenger, to those who believe and do righteous deeds, good tidings that will fill them with joy: that for them in the Hereafter are wondrous gardens beneath which rivers flow, with lofty palaces and shady trees. Whenever they are provided with a kind of delicious fruit therein, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," yet when they taste it they will find it something new in its taste and delight, even though it resembles its predecessor in color, appearance and name. For them in the Gardens are spouses purified from every kind of sensory impurity, such as urine and menstruation, and every kind of moral impurity, such as lying and bad character. And they will abide eternally in the Garden and its bliss, never dying therein and never being removed from it.

Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, is not shy of stating the truth, whether it be something small or great, even if the illustration is with the smallest of things, such as the gnat and the fly and the like, which Allah has struck as a parable for the powerlessness of everything that is worshipped besides Allah. As for the believers, they know the wisdom of Allah in giving examples with the small and the great of His creation. As for the disbelievers, they mock and say: What does Allah intend by striking a parable with these worthless insects? Allah answers them that the purpose is trial and the distinguishing of the believer from the disbeliever. Therefore, through this parable Allah leads many people astray from the truth because of their mockery of it, and through it He grants success to others, guiding them to greater faith and guidance. And Allah, exalted is He, does not wrong anyone, for He only misguides those who have departed from His obedience.

Those who break the covenant of Allah after it has been established, which He took from them to affirm monotheism and obedience, and which He confirmed by sending the messengers and revealing the scriptures, and who oppose the religion of Allah by severing the ties of kinship and spreading corruption on the earth: those are the losers, in this world and in the Hereafter.

How can you disbelieve in God, O polytheists, and associate others with Him in worship, when the decisive proof of His oneness lies within yourselves? You were non-existent, and He brought you into being and breathed life into you. Then He will cause you to die when your appointed terms, which He has set for you, have come to an end. Then He will restore you to life on the Day of Resurrection. Then to Him you will be returned for reckoning and recompense.

God alone is the One who created for your sake everything on the earth, the bounties from which you benefit. Then He turned His intent to the heavens, and fashioned them as seven heavens, and He is All-Knowing of everything. So His knowledge, glorified is He, encompasses all that He has created.

And mention, O Messenger, to the people, when your Lord said to the angels: "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive generation (khalifah)," to inhabit it and cultivate it. They said: "Our Lord, teach us and guide us as to what wisdom there is in creating these, when among their traits is corruption on the earth and the shedding of blood unjustly and aggressively, while we are obedient to Your command, glorifying You with the glorification befitting Your praise and Your majesty, and extolling You with every attribute of perfection and magnificence?" God said to them: "Indeed, I know what you do not know of the overriding benefit in their creation."

To show the excellence of Adam (peace be upon him), Allah taught him the names of all things. Then He presented their referents (musammayatuha) to the angels, saying to them: "Inform Me of the names of these beings, if you are truthful in your claim that you are more deserving of being vicegerents on the earth than they are."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 49:

Remember Our favour upon you when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to the worst torment: they would slaughter your sons in great numbers and let your women live to serve and be humiliated. In that was a trial from your Lord, and in your deliverance from it lies a great blessing, which calls for thanking Allah in every age and generation of yours.

Remember Our favor upon you when We divided the sea for you, so you passed through it, and We rescued you from Pharaoh's people and drowned them before your eyes. (Note: the translation follows the text as given.)

Let me correct that and give the full translation faithfully:

Remember Our blessing upon you when We parted the sea on your account, and made in it dry paths, so you crossed over, and We rescued you from Pharaoh and his soldiers, and from destruction in the water. Then when Pharaoh and his soldiers entered your path, We drowned them in the water before your eyes.

Remember Our favour upon you when We appointed for Moses forty nights [for the descent of the Torah, a guidance and a light for you]. Then, behold, you took the calf [as a deity] in his absence, [though] you were wrongdoers.

Wait, I should translate the passage itself, not the verse alone. Here is the full translation:

Remember Our favour upon you when We appointed for Moses forty nights for the revelation of the Torah, a guidance and a light for you. Then you seized the opportunity of his absence during this short period, and made the calf that you had fashioned with your own hands an object of worship besides Allah—and this is the most abominable form of disbelief in Allah—while you were wrongdoers in taking the calf as a god.

Then We pardoned you for that grave transgression and accepted your repentance after Moses' return, so that perhaps you would give thanks to God for His blessings and favors, and not persist in disbelief and rebellion.

Remember the blessing We bestowed upon you when We gave Musa (Moses) the Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, which is the Tawrat (Torah), so that you may be guided away from misguidance.

Remember Our favour upon you when Moses said to his people: "Indeed you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf as a deity, so turn in repentance to your Creator, by having some of you kill others. That is better for you with your Creator than everlasting abiding in the Fire." And you complied with that, so Allah bestowed His favour upon you by accepting your repentance. Indeed, He is the Ever-Accepting of repentance from whoever repents among His servants, the Most Merciful toward them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 55:

And remember when you said: "O Musa, we will not believe you that the speech we hear from you is the speech of Allah until we see Allah plainly with our own eyes." So the destroying punishment seized you, the very one you witnessed with your own eyes, and it killed you because of your sins and your audacity against Allah, the Exalted.

Then We revived you after your death (caused by the thunderbolt), so that you might give thanks for the favor of Allah upon you. This death was a punishment for them; then Allah raised them up to complete their appointed terms.

Remember Our blessing upon you when you wandered in the wilderness, when We made the clouds cast shade over you against the heat of the sun, and sent down upon you al-Mann, a substance resembling gum, whose taste is like honey, and sent down upon you al-Salwa, a bird resembling the quail. And We said to you: "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you, but do not defy your religion," yet you did not comply. They did not wrong Us by ungratefulness for the blessings, but rather they wronged themselves, because the consequence of wrongdoing returns upon them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 58:

So the wrongdoers and the misguided among the Children of Israel changed the word of God, and they distorted both the statement and the action. They entered crawling on their buttocks and said: "A grain in a hair," and they mocked the religion of God. So God sent down upon them a punishment from the sky, because of their rebellion and their departure from obedience to God.

Remember Our blessing upon you when you were thirsty in the wilderness of wandering (al-tih), when Moses humbly supplicated Us to give water to his people. So We said: "Strike the rock with your staff," and he struck it, and from it burst forth twelve springs, corresponding to the number of tribes, each tribe being made aware of its own spring so that they would not dispute with one another. And We said to them: "Eat and drink of the provision of God, and do not go about the earth spreading corruption."

Remember when We sent down to you manna and quail, the sweet food and the delicious bird. But you grew ungrateful for the blessing, as was your habit, and hardship and boredom afflicted you, so you said: "O Moses, we will not be patient with one kind of food that never changes over the days. So pray to your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs and its vegetables, its cucumbers, its grains that are eaten, its lentils, and its onions." Moses said, disapproving of them: "Do you ask for these foods, which are of lesser worth, in exchange for that which is better? Go down to any city, and you will find what you have asked for in abundance in the fields and markets." When they went down, it became clear that they put their own choice, in every situation, ahead of God's choice, and preferred their desires over what God had chosen for them. Therefore the mark of humiliation and poverty of spirit clung to them, and they returned bearing anger from God, because of their turning away from the religion of God, and because they used to disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the prophets unjustly and aggressively; and that was due to their disobedience and their transgression of the limits set by their Lord.

Indeed, the believers of this nation, who affirmed belief in Allah and His messengers and acted upon His law, and those who were before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) from the earlier nations, among the Jews, the Christians, and the Sabians (al-Sabi'un) — and they are a people who remain upon their natural disposition (fitrah), with no established religion for them to follow — all of these, if they affirmed belief in Allah with a sound and sincere affirmation, and in the Day of Resurrection and recompense, and did a deed that is pleasing to Allah, then their reward is secure for them with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them regarding what they will face of the matters of the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over what they missed of the matters of this world. As for after the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), as the seal of the prophets and messengers sent to all of mankind, Allah will not accept from anyone a religion other than what he brought, and that is Islam.

Remember, O Children of Israel, when We took your solemn covenant to believe in God and to worship Him alone, and raised Mount Sinai above you, and said to you: "Take hold of the Book that We have given you with determination and diligence, and keep it in memory. Otherwise, We will bring the mountain down upon you." And do not forget the Torah, in word and in deed, so that you may be mindful of Me and fear My punishment.

Then you broke your word and disobeyed once again, after the covenant was taken and the mountain was raised over you, as is your constant habit. Had it not been for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy in accepting your repentance and overlooking your sins, you would surely have been among the losers in this world and the Hereafter.

And you have certainly known, O People of the Book (Jews), what calamity befell your forefathers, the people of the town who disobeyed God's command regarding their obligation to honor the Sabbath. They devised a trick to catch fish on the Sabbath day by setting up nets and digging pools, and then they caught the fish on Sunday, as a stratagem to get around what was forbidden. When they did this, God transformed them into apes, cast out and despised.

So We made this town an example for those in its vicinity of the other towns, whose report reaches them and what befell it, and an example for those who would later commit sins like those. We also made it a reminder for the righteous, so that they might know that they are upon the truth and remain steadfast upon it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 67:

Remember, O Children of Israel, the wrongdoing of your forefathers and their great obstinacy and disputation with Musa (peace be upon him), when he said to them: "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 69:

So they returned to their argument, saying: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us its color." He said: "Indeed, He says it is a yellow cow, intensely yellow in its color, pleasing to whoever looks upon it."

The Children of Israel said to Musa: "Call upon your Lord for us that He may clarify for us other attributes beyond those mentioned before, for cattle with these attributes are many, so it has become confusing to us which one to choose. They said: "Now you have brought the true description of the cow." So they were compelled to slaughter it after much evasion, and they had nearly not done so, out of their obstinacy. Thus they made it difficult for themselves, so Allah made it difficult for them.

And remember when you killed a soul and then disputed over it, each of you deflecting from himself the accusation of the killing. But Allah is the One who brings out what you were concealing of the killing of the slain man.

So We said: "Strike the slain man with a piece of this slaughtered cow; Allah will bring him back to life and inform you of his killer." They struck him with part of it, and Allah brought him back to life and he informed them of his killer. Thus Allah will bring the dead back to life on the Day of Resurrection, and He will show you, O Children of Israel, His miracles that indicate His perfect power, so that you may reflect with your minds and refrain from His disobedience.

But you did not benefit from that. Despite all these extraordinary miracles, your hearts became hardened and coarse, so no good could penetrate them, and they did not soften before the striking signs that We showed you, until your hearts became like hard stones, nay, they are even harsher in hardness. For among stones there are those that expand and open up until water gushes forth from them in torrents, so that they become flowing rivers; and among stones there are those that split open and crack, so that springs and fountains emerge from them; and among stones there are those that fall from the heights of mountains out of fear of God Most High and reverence for Him. ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do.﴾

O Muslims, have you forgotten the deeds of the Children of Israel, so that your souls hope that the Jews will believe in your religion? Their scholars used to hear the words of God from the Torah, and then they would distort them, either by diverting them to a meaning other than their correct one after they had understood their true sense, or by altering their wording, while they knew that they were deliberately and falsely distorting the words of the Lord of the worlds.

These Jews, when they meet those who believe, say with their tongues: "We believe in your religion and your Messenger, who is foretold in the Torah." But when some of these hypocritical Jews are alone with one another, they say in denial: "Do you tell the believers what Allah has made clear to you in the Torah about the matter of Muhammad, so that they may have the proof against you before your Lord on the Day of Resurrection? Do you not understand, so that you might be cautious?"
Do they commit all these crimes while failing to realize that Allah knows everything they conceal and everything they reveal?

Among the Jews is a group who cannot read or write, and they do not know the Torah or what it contains of the descriptions of the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). What they have of it is nothing but falsehoods and corrupt assumptions.

Woe and severe punishment to the evil rabbis among the Jews who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," while it contradicts what Allah revealed to His Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, in order to take in exchange for this a little of the goods of this world. So they will have a destructive punishment because of their writing this falsehood with their own hands, and they will have a destructive punishment because of what they take in return of wealth that is unlawful, such as bribery and other things.

The Children of Israel said: "The Fire will not touch us in the Hereafter except for a few numbered days." Say to them, O Messenger, refuting their claim: "Do you have a covenant from God concerning this, for God never breaks His covenant? Rather, you are saying about God what you do not know, by fabricating falsehood."

Thus the judgment of Allah is established: whoever commits sins until they drag him into disbelief, and his sins take control of him from every side (and this only happens to one who associates partners with Allah), those are the polytheists and disbelievers who will abide in the Fire of Hell in a constant abiding that never ends.

The ruling of God that stands in contrast to this is: those who believed in God and His messengers with sincere belief, and who did deeds that accord with the law of God which He revealed to His messengers, these will abide in Paradise in the Hereafter, an abiding that is never cut off.

And remember, O Children of Israel, when We took a firm covenant from you: that you would worship Allah alone, without associating anything with Him; that you would be good to parents, to relatives, to orphans whose fathers have died while they are still below the age of puberty, and to the needy who do not own what suffices them and meets their need; that you would speak good words to people; and that you would establish the prayer and give the zakat. Then you turned away and broke the covenant, except for a few of you who remained steadfast upon it, while you continued in your turning away.

Remember, O Children of Israel, when We took a binding covenant from you in the Torah: that you would not shed one another's blood, nor expel one another from your homes. Then you acknowledged this, and you were witnesses to its truth.

Then you, O people, kill one another and expel one another from their homes, and each group among you supports its allies against their brethren with the enemy, out of injustice and aggression. And if they come to you as captives in the hands of the enemy, you strive to free them from captivity by paying the ransom, although it is forbidden for you to expel them from their homes. How evil is what you do, when you believe in some of the rulings of the Torah and disbelieve in others! So the recompense of whoever among you does that is nothing but humiliation and disgrace in this world. And on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will return them to the most severe punishment in the Fire. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.

Those are the ones who preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter. So their punishment will not be lightened for them, and they will have no helper to defend them against the punishment of Allah.

We certainly gave Moses the Torah, and We sent after him a succession of messengers from the Children of Israel. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear miracles, and We strengthened him with Jibril (peace be upon him). Is it, then, that whenever a messenger came to you with revelation from Allah that did not suit your desires, you grew arrogant and rejected some of them, and killed others?

This is the commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 88, from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

The Children of Israel said to the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ): "Our hearts are covered; your words do not penetrate them." But the matter is not as they claimed. Rather, their hearts are cursed, sealed over, and they are expelled from the mercy of Allah because of their denial, so they will not believe except with a little faith that will not benefit them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 89:

When there came to them the Qur'an from Allah, confirming what was with them of the Torah, they disbelieved in it and denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Before his mission, they used to seek victory through him against the polytheists of Arabia, saying: "The time of the prophet of the last age has drawn near, and we will follow him and fight you alongside him." But when there came to them the Messenger whose attributes and truthfulness they recognised, they disbelieved in him and denied him. So the curse of Allah is upon everyone who disbelieves in the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in His Book which Allah revealed to him.

Evil is what the Children of Israel have chosen for themselves, for they exchanged disbelief for belief out of wrongdoing and envy at God's sending down the Qur'an, by His bounty, upon the Prophet of God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). So they returned bearing wrath from God upon them, because of their denial of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in addition to the wrath of God upon them likewise for their distortion of the Torah. For those who deny the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) there is a punishment that will humiliate and disgrace them.

When some of the believers say to the Jews, "Believe in what Allah has sent down, the Qur'an," they reply, "We believe in what was sent down to us, to our prophets," and they reject what Allah has sent down after that, which is the truth confirming what is with them. If they truly believed in their scriptures, they would believe in the Qur'an, which confirms them. Say to them, O Messenger: If you are believers in what was sent down to you, then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before?

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 92:

Moses, the Prophet of Allah, came to you with clear miracles that testify to his truthfulness, such as the flood, the locusts, the lice, and the frogs, and other things that Allah mentioned in the Mighty Qur'an. Yet despite this, you took the calf as a deity to worship, after Moses had gone to the appointed time with his Lord, while you were transgressing the limits of Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 93:

Remember when We took your covenant and raised above you Mount Sinai, saying: "Hold firmly to what We have given you, and listen and obey." But you said: "We hear and we disobey." Their hearts had absorbed the worship of the calf because of their persistence in disbelief. Say, [O Messenger]: "Evil is what your faith commands you to do, of disbelief and misguidance, if you are [truly] believers in what Allah has sent down to you."

Say, [O Messenger], to the Jews who claim that Paradise is exclusively theirs, because they assert that they are the friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people, and that they are His sons and His beloved ones: If the matter is as you claim, then invoke death upon the liars among you or among others, if you are truthful in this claim of yours.

This is the commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 95 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

And they will never wish for it (death), because of what they know of the truthfulness of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and of their own lying and fabrication, and because of what they have committed of disbelief and disobedience, which lead to their being deprived of Paradise and entering the Fire. And Allah, the Exalted, is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers among His servants, and He will recompense them for that.

And you will surely find, O Messenger, that the Jews are the most eager of people for a long life, whatever that life may be of humiliation and degradation. Their eagerness for long life even exceeds that of the polytheists. A Jew wishes to live a thousand years, and this long life, should he attain it, will not keep him away from the punishment of Allah. Allah, exalted is He, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for them with the punishment they deserve.

Say, O Messenger, to the Jews when they said, "Gabriel is our enemy among the angels": whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then indeed he it is who sent down the Qur'an upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what came before it of the books of Allah, and as a guide to the truth, and as a bearer of good news to those who believe in it of every good in this world and the Hereafter.

Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and messengers, whether from among the angels or mankind, and especially the two angels Jibril (Gabriel) and Mikail (Michael); this is because the Jews claimed that Jibril was their enemy and Mikail was their ally. So Allah informed them that whoever is an enemy to one of these two has thereby become an enemy to the other, and is also an enemy to Allah, for Allah is an enemy to those who deny what He sent down to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

And We have certainly sent down to you, O Messenger, clear and manifest signs, which indicate that you are truly and genuinely a messenger from Allah. None deny those signs except those who have departed from the religion of Allah.

How ugly is the state of the Children of Israel in their breaking of covenants! Whenever they make a covenant, a group among them casts that covenant aside and breaks it. You see them ratifying a covenant today and breaking it tomorrow. Indeed, most of them do not believe in what the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), brought.

When Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), came to them with the Qur'an, which agreed with what they already had of the Torah, a group of them cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, acting like the ignorant who do not know its truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 102:

Ruling the translation: the Arabic passage is a tafsir text, so I translate it sentence by sentence, keeping Qur'anic quotations in ﴿ ﴾ and transliterating technical terms with glosses on first use.

The Jews followed what the devils recited to the sorcerers during the reign of Solomon, son of David. Solomon did not disbelieve, nor did he learn sorcery; rather, it was the devils who disbelieved in God, when they taught people sorcery, corrupting their religion. Likewise, the Jews followed the sorcery that was sent down to the two angels Harut and Marut in the land of "Babylon" in "Iraq," as a trial and test from God for His servants. The two angels would not teach anyone until they had advised him and warned him against learning sorcery, saying to him: "Do not disbelieve by learning sorcery and obeying the devils." People would then learn from the two angels that by which they cause enmity between a husband and wife, so that they separate. Yet the sorcerers cannot harm anyone with it except by God's permission and decree. What the sorcerers learn harms them and does not benefit them, and the devils conveyed it to the Jews, and it spread among them until they preferred it over the Book of God. The Jews certainly knew that whoever chooses sorcery and abandons the truth has no share of good in the Hereafter. Wretched is what they sold their souls for, namely sorcery and disbelief in exchange for faith and following the Messenger (ﷺ), if only they had knowledge that would produce action in accordance with what they were admonished with.

If the Jews had believed and feared Allah, they would have been certain that Allah's reward is better for them than the magic and what they gained by it. If only they had known what comes from faith and God-consciousness of reward and recompense, with true knowledge, they would have believed.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 104:

O you who have believed, do not say to the Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), "Raina" (ra'ina), meaning: "Raina samʿaka" (give heed to us), that is: understand what we say, and make us understand. This is because the Jews used to say it to the Prophet (ﷺ), twisting their tongues with it, intending to revile him and to ascribe to him foolishness (ruʿūna). Say instead, O believers, in its place: "Unzurna" (look at us), that is: look upon us and take care of us; it conveys the very same intended meaning. And listen to what is recited to you from the Book of your Lord and understand it. And for those who deny, there is a painful punishment.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 105:

Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord, (not even) the least of it, whether the Qur'an, knowledge, victory, or good tidings. But Allah singles out for His mercy whomever He wills of His servants, with prophethood and messengership. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty and abundant, vast giving.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 106:

We do not abrogate any verse or cause it to be forgotten from hearts and minds, but We bring one better for you than it, or one like it in obligation and reward. And each has its wisdom. Do you not know, O Prophet, you and your nation, that Allah is All-Powerful, nothing can overcome Him?

Have you not known, O Prophet, you and your nation, that Allah, exalted is He, is the Owner and the Disposer of the heavens and the earth? He does what He wills, and decrees what He desires, and commands His servants and forbids them however He wishes, and they must obey and accept. And let those who disobey know that there is no protector besides Allah who will take charge of them, nor any helper who will prevent them from the punishment of Allah.

Rather, do you wish, O people, to ask your Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) for things out of obstinate defiance, just as such demands were made of Musa (Moses) before? Know that whoever chooses disbelief and abandons faith has strayed from the straight path of Allah into ignorance and misguidance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 109:

Many of the People of the Book wish that they could turn you back into disbelievers after your faith, just as you were before, worshipping idols, out of the spite that has filled their souls after it has become clear to them that the Prophet of God and His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), speaks the truth in what he has brought. So pardon what they have done of harm and error, and overlook their ignorance, until God brings His command concerning them, by fighting them (and it has come and occurred), and He will punish them for the evil of their deeds. Indeed, God is over all things capable; nothing can overpower Him.

Be occupied, O believers, with performing the prayer in its proper form and giving the obligatory zakat. And know that every good deed you send ahead for yourselves, you will find its reward with Allah in the Hereafter. Indeed, He, may He be exalted, is All-Seeing of all your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

Each of the Jews and the Christians claimed that Paradise is exclusive to their own group, and that no one else will enter it. These are their corrupt delusions. Say to them, O Messenger: "Bring your proof for the soundness of what you claim, if you are truthful in your claim."

The matter is not as they claim, that Paradise is exclusive to a particular group apart from others. Rather, whoever submits himself entirely to Allah alone, with no partner associated with Him, and follows the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in all his sayings and deeds, will enter Paradise. Whoever does this will have the reward of his deed with his Lord in the Hereafter, which is entry into Paradise. They will have no fear regarding what they face of the matters of the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over what they have missed of the portions of this worldly life.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 113:

And the Jews said: "The Christians are not upon anything of the correct religion." And likewise the Christians said of the Jews, while they recite the Torah and the Gospel, and in both of them is the obligation of faith in all the prophets. Thus said those who have no knowledge, from the polytheists of the Arabs and others, something similar to their saying; that is, they said to every follower of a religion: "You are upon nothing." So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning what they differed about regarding the matter of religion, and will recompense each one according to his deeds.

No one is more unjust than those who prevent the remembrance of Allah in the mosques, from establishing the prayer, reciting the Qur'an, and the like, and who strive to ruin them by demolishing them, closing them, or preventing the believers from entering them. Those are the wrongdoers; it was not fitting for them to enter the mosques except in fear and trepidation of punishment. For them, in this world, is humiliation and disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is severe punishment.

To Allah belong the east and the west, and whatever lies between them. He is the Owner of the whole earth. So wherever you turn to in prayer by the command of Allah, you are seeking His Face; you have not gone outside His dominion and obedience. Indeed Allah is All-Encompassing in mercy toward His servants, All-Knowing of their deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

The Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists said: "God has taken a son for Himself." Glory be to God, exalted above this false statement. Rather, everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him as His possession and His servants, and they are all humbly subject to Him, subjected to His governance.

This is the commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2:117):

Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth without any prior pattern or model. And when He decrees a matter and wills its existence, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 118:

The ignorant ones among the People of the Book and others said to the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), out of obstinacy: "Why does Allah not speak to us directly to inform us that you are His Messenger? Or why does a sign (mu'jizah) from Allah not come to us that indicates the truth of what you say?" A similar statement was made by the nations before them to their messengers, out of obstinacy and arrogance; this is because the hearts of the earlier and later generations are alike in disbelief and misguidance. We have already made the signs clear for those who believe with firm conviction, because they are believers in Allah, the Exalted, following what He has prescribed for them.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 119:

We have sent you, O Messenger, with the true religion, supported by proofs and miracles. So convey it to the people, along with giving good news to the believers of the good of both this world and the Hereafter, and warning the obstinate deniers of what awaits them of the punishment of Allah. You are not, after conveying the message, responsible for the disbelief of those who disbelieve in you, for they will enter the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and will not come out of it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 120:

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, [O Messenger], nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾ Say: "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance." And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have against Allah no protector or helper.

And this address, although it is specifically directed to the Prophet (ﷺ), is directed to the Ummah in general.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 121:

Those whom We gave the Book, from among the Jews and the Christians, who recite it with the correct recitation, follow it with the truest following, and believe in what it contains of belief in the messengers of God, among them their final seal, our Prophet and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and who do not distort or alter what it contains. These are the ones who believe in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what was revealed to him. As for those who altered part of the Book and concealed part of it, these are disbelievers in the Prophet of God Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what was revealed to him. Whoever disbelieves in him, those are the greatest of people in loss before God.
O children of Israel, remember My numerous blessings upon you, and that I preferred you over the peoples of your time by sending many prophets among you and revealing scriptures to them.

And fear the terrors of the Day of Reckoning, when no soul will avail another soul in anything. Allah will not accept from it any ransom that would save it from punishment, nor will any intercession benefit it, nor will anyone come to its aid.

Remember, O Prophet, when Allah tested Ibrahim (Abraham) with the duties He had prescribed for him, and he fulfilled them and carried them out in the best manner. Allah said to him: "Indeed, I will make you a leader for mankind." Ibrahim said: "My Lord, make some of my offspring leaders, out of Your bounty." Allah answered him, glorified is He, that leadership in religion will not be attained by the wrongdoers.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 125:

Mention, O Prophet, when We made the Ka'bah a place of return for the people, who come to it and then return to their families and then come back to it again, and a gathering place for them for the Hajj, the 'Umrah, and the circumambulation (tawaf) and prayer, and a sanctuary for them, where no enemy raids them within it. And We said: "Take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer," and it is the stone on which Abraham stood when he was building the Ka'bah. And We inspired to Abraham and his son Isma'il: "Purify My House from every filth and impurity, for those who worship in it by circumambulating the Ka'bah, or by staying in seclusion (i'tikaf) in the mosque, and by praying in it."

You, O Prophet, should recall when Ibrahim said in supplication: "My Lord, make this city (Makkah) a secure land, free from fear, and provide its people with fruits of all kinds, and specially grant this provision to those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day." Allah said: "As for those who disbelieve among them, I will provide for them in this worldly life and let them enjoy it for a little, then I will compel them, against their will, to the torment of the Fire. And wretched is that destination."

And mention, O Prophet, when Ibrahim and Isma'il were raising the foundations of the Ka'bah, while they supplicated Allah in humility: "Our Lord, accept from us our good deeds and our supplication. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing of the words of Your servants, the All-Knowing of their circumstances."

Our Lord, make us both steadfast in Islam, submissive to Your rulings. Make from our offspring a community submissive to You, through faith. Show us the landmarks of our worship of You, and pardon our sins. Indeed, You are the One who accepts repentance abundantly from Your servants, and vast in mercy toward them.

Our Lord, and send among this community a messenger from the descendants of Ismail, who will recite to them Your verses, teach them the Book (the Qur'an) and the Sunnah (the way and practice of the Prophet ﷺ), and purify them from shirk (associating partners with Allah) and bad conduct. Indeed You are the Almighty, whom nothing can resist, the All-Wise, who places things in their proper places.

No one turns away from the religion of Ibrahim, which is Islam, except a foolish ignorant person. We indeed chose Ibrahim in this world as a prophet and messenger, and he, in the Hereafter, is certainly among the righteous, who will have the highest ranks.

The reason for this choice was his swift acceptance of Islam without hesitation, when his Lord said to him: ﴿Submit,﴾ that is, devote yourself sincerely to Allah, submitting to Him. So Ibrahim responded and said: ﴿I have submitted myself to the Lord of the worlds,﴾ with sincerity, monotheism, love, and turning back to Him in repentance.

Ibrahim and Ya'qub (Jacob) urged their sons to hold firm to Islam, saying: "O our sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, which is the religion of Islam, so do not abandon it throughout your lives, and do not let death overtake you except while you are upon it."

Were you present, O Jews, when death came to Ya'qub (Jacob)? [Remember] when he gathered his sons and asked them: "What will you worship after I am gone?" They said: "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim (Abraham), Isma'il (Ishmael) and Ishaq (Isaac), one God, and to Him we submit in obedience."

This is the commentary on Qur'an 2:134 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the "Simplified Tafsir" of King Fahd Complex). However, the passage you provided is the Qur'anic verse itself, not the commentary. Here is its translation, with the Qur'anic text rendered within ﴿ ﴾ markers as required:

Note: The text you sent, however, reads as a paraphrase rather than the verse in its standard form. Here is the translation of the text exactly as given:

That is a nation from your forefathers that has passed away. For them is what they earned, and for you is what you earn, and you will not be asked about what they did, and they will not be asked about what you do, and each will be recompensed for what he did, no one will be taken to account for the sin of another, and nothing will benefit anyone except his faith and his piety.

The Jews said to the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ): "Enter into the religion of Judaism and you will be guided." The Christians said the same to them. Say to them, O Messenger: "Rather, guidance lies in all of us following the millah (religious creed) of Ibrahim (Abraham), who turned away from every false religion to the religion of truth, and who was not among those who associated partners with God, Exalted is He."

Say, O believers, to these Jews and Christians: "We believe in God, the One who alone is truly worthy of worship, and in what has been revealed to us, the Qur'an, which God revealed to His Prophet and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in what was revealed in the scrolls to Abraham, and to his two sons Ishmael and Isaac, and to Jacob, and to the Tribes (al-Asbat), who are the prophets from among the descendants of Jacob, who were among the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel, and in what was given to Moses of the Torah, and to Jesus of the Gospel, and in what was given to all the prophets from their Lord's revelation. We do not make any distinction between any one of them in faith, and we are submissive to God in obedience and worship."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 137:

If the disbelievers among the Jews, the Christians and others believe in the like of what you have believed in, of what the Messenger brought, then they have been guided to the truth. But if they turn away, then they are only in severe discord. So Allah will suffice you, O Messenger, against their evil and will give you victory over them. And He is the All-Hearing of your words, the All-Knowing of your conditions.

Hold fast to the religion of God, which He has instilled in you as your natural disposition (fitrah). There is nothing better than the natural disposition of God upon which He created people, so hold fast to it, and say: "We are submissive to Him and obedient to our Lord, following the creed (millah) of Abraham."

Say, [O Messenger], to the People of the Book: Do you argue with us about the Oneness of Allah and sincerity to Him, when He is the Lord of all the worlds, not specific to one people over another? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we are sincere to Allah in worship and obedience, associating nothing with Him and worshipping none other than Him?

Nay, do you say, disputing about God, that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes (al-Asbat), who are the prophets from the descendants of Jacob, who were among the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel, were Jews or Christians? This is a lie, for they were sent and died before the Torah and the Gospel were revealed. Say to them, O Messenger: Are you more knowing of their religion, or is God Most High? He has informed in the Qur'an that they were ḥanīfs (upright monotheists) and muslims (submitters to God), and there is no one more unjust than you, who conceal a testimony established with you from God Most High, and claim the opposite of it, fabricating against God. And God is not unaware of anything of your deeds; rather, He counts them and will recompense you for them.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 2:141 from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex):

That community (ummah) of your forebears has passed away. They have what they earned, and you have what you earn. You will not be questioned about what they did, nor will they be questioned about what you do. The verse cuts off reliance on created beings, and warns against being deceived by lineage to them; what matters is faith in God, worshipping Him alone, and following His messengers. And whoever disbelieves in one of their messengers has disbelieved in all the messengers.

The Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 2, verse 142:

Those who are foolish and weak of mind among the Jews and their likes will say, in mockery and objection: "What has turned these Muslims away from their qibla, the one they used to face in prayer at the beginning of Islam?" (That qibla was Bayt al-Maqdis, Jerusalem.) Say to them, O Messenger: "To God belongs the east and the west and whatever lies between them. No direction is outside His dominion, and He guides whomever He wills of His servants to the straight path of guidance." In this there is an indication that the whole matter belongs to God in obeying His commands: wherever He directs us, we turn.

Just as We guided you, O Muslims, to the correct path in religion, We made you a community of the best and most just, so that you may bear witness against the nations on the Day of Judgment that their messengers conveyed to them the messages of their Lord, and that the Messenger (ﷺ) will likewise bear witness against you that he conveyed to you the message of his Lord. And We did not make the direction of prayer that you were facing, O Messenger, the qiblah of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), except so that what We had known from eternity would become manifest, a knowledge upon which reward and punishment depend; so that We might distinguish those who follow you, obey you, and face the direction with you wherever you turn, from those who are weak in faith and turn back as apostates from their religion because of their doubt and hypocrisy. This change, in which the Muslim turns in prayer from facing Bayt al-Maqdis to facing the Ka'bah, is indeed a heavy and difficult matter, except for those whom Allah has guided and favored with faith and piety. Allah would not cause your faith in Him and your following of His Messenger to be lost, nor nullify your prayers toward the former qiblah. Indeed, He, glorified and exalted, is Most Merciful to people with a vast mercy, in their present life and in their life to come.

We see your face, O Messenger, turning toward the sky again and again, awaiting the revelation concerning the qibla. So We shall surely turn you to a qibla that you love and are pleased with: it is the direction of the Sacred Mosque in Makkah, so turn your face toward it. Wherever you are, O Muslims, and whenever you intend to pray, turn toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, those who were given knowledge of the Book among the Jews and Christians certainly know that the turning to the Ka'bah is the truth established in their scriptures. And Allah is not unaware of what these objectors and doubters do, and He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 145:

Even if you brought, O Messenger, to those who were given the Torah and the Gospel every sign and proof that your turning toward the Ka'bah in prayer is the truth from Allah, they would not follow your qiblah, out of obstinacy and arrogance. Nor are you one who will follow their qiblah again, and some of them are not followers of the qiblah of others. And if you were to follow their desires concerning the qiblah and other matters after the knowledge that has come to you, that you are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood, then indeed you would then be of the wrongdoers toward yourself. This is an address to the whole Ummah, and it is a warning and a threat to whoever follows the desires of those who oppose the Shari'ah of Islam.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 146:

Those to whom We gave the Torah and the Gospel recognize him (Muhammad ﷺ) as the Messenger of Allah, through his attributes mentioned in their scriptures, just as they recognize their own sons. Yet indeed a group of them conceal the truth while they know its veracity and the establishment of his attributes.

The truth that has been sent down to you, O Prophet, is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt it. Although this is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ), it is directed to the community (ummah).

This is a commentary passage (tafsir al-Muyassar, i.e., the King Fahd Complex's "al-Tafsir al-Muyassar") on Qur'an 2:148. Translating:

Every nation has a direction (qiblah) toward which each one of them turns in their prayer. So hasten, O believers, competing with one another to perform the righteous deeds that Allah has prescribed for you in the religion of Islam. Allah will gather you all together on the Day of Resurrection from wherever you may be. Indeed, Allah is over all things capable.

And from wherever you set out, O Prophet, on a journey, and you wish to pray, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, your turning toward it is the truth established from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do, and He will recompense you for that.

From whatever place you set out, O Prophet, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, O Muslims, in whatever region of the earth you may be, turn your faces toward the Sacred Mosque, so that the people who oppose you will have no argument against you by way of dispute and contention after this turning toward it, except those among them who are unjust and obstinate. They will continue in their disputing, so do not fear them, but fear Me by complying with My command and avoiding My prohibition; and so that I may complete My favor upon you by choosing for you the most perfect of laws, and so that you may be guided to the truth and what is right.

As We have bestowed upon you the favor of facing the Ka'bah, We have sent among you a Messenger from yourselves, who recites to you the verses that make clear the truth from falsehood, purifies you from the defilement of polytheism and bad conduct, teaches you the Book (al-Kitab) and the Sunnah and the rulings of the Sharia (religious law), and teaches you news of the prophets and the stories of the earlier nations, which you used to be ignorant of.

God commanded the believers to remember Him, and promised for this the best reward: that He would praise, in the exalted assembly, the one who remembers Him. "And be grateful to Me, [by word and deed], and do not deny Me [i.e., do not be ungrateful for My blessings upon you]."

O you who believe, seek help from Allah in all your affairs: through patience in the face of calamities and misfortunes, through patience in abstaining from sins and wrongdoings, through patience in acts of obedience and drawing near to Allah, and through prayer, by which the soul finds tranquility and which forbids indecency and wrongdoing. Indeed, Allah is with the patient, with His help, His success, and His support. In the verse is an affirmation of Allah's special companionship (ma'iyyah) with the believers, which entails what has been mentioned above. As for the general companionship, which entails knowledge and encompassing, it is for all of creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 154:

And do not say, O believers, about those who are killed in the way of Allah while striving (mujahidin): they are dead. Rather, they are alive, with a life特 peculiar to them in their graves, the manner of which none knows but Allah, the Exalted, but you do not perceive it. In this is evidence for the bliss of the grave.

We will surely test you with a little fear, hunger, loss of wealth through difficulty in obtaining it or its being taken away, loss of lives through death or martyrdom in the way of Allah, and loss of fruits, dates, grapes and grain through their yield being scant or spoiled. But give good tidings, O Prophet, to those who are patient in the face of these and similar trials, with what will gladden them and delight them: a good outcome in this world and the Hereafter.

Among the attributes of these patient ones is that when something they dislike befalls them, they say: "Indeed, we belong to Allah, as His servants who are owned and ordered by His command and disposal; He does with us what He wills. And indeed, to Him we will return by death, and then by resurrection for reckoning and recompense."
Those are the patient. They have praise from their Lord and great mercy from Him, glory be to Him, and those are the ones who are guided to right conduct.

Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwa, which are two small hills near the Ka'bah on its eastern side, are among the manifest symbols (sha'a'ir) of God's religion, through which God has commanded His servants to perform sa'y (the ritual running between them). So whoever intends the Ka'bah for hajj or 'umrah, there is no sin upon him and no fault in his going back and forth between them; rather, doing so is obligatory for him. And whoever performs acts of obedience voluntarily, from his own self, sincerely for God Most High, then indeed God is Shakur (the Appreciative), who rewards the little with much, and He is 'Alim (the All-Knowing) of the deeds of His servants, so He does not waste them, nor does He diminish for anyone even the weight of an atom.

Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of the clear signs that point to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and to what he brought, and they are the rabbis of the Jews, the scholars of the Christians, and others who hide what Allah has sent down after We have made it manifest to the people in the Torah and the Gospel — those, Allah banishes them from His mercy, and all of creation curses them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 160:

Except for those who turn back in repentance, seek forgiveness from Allah for their sins, set right what they had corrupted, and make clear what they had concealed. As for them, I accept their repentance and reward them with forgiveness, and I am the Accepter of repentance from whoever of My servants repents, the Most Merciful towards them, for I have granted them success in repentance and accepted it from them.

Indeed, those who disbelieved, concealed the truth, and persisted in that until they died, upon them is the curse of Allah, meaning their expulsion from His mercy, and upon them is the curse of the angels and of all of mankind.
Abiding forever in the curse and the Fire. Their punishment will not be lightened, and they will not be given respite to offer an excuse.

Your God, O people, is one God, singular in His essence, His names, His attributes, and His actions, and in the worship of His creation toward Him. There is no one worthy of worship except Him: the Most Gracious (al-Rahman), characterized by mercy in His essence and His actions toward all creation, the Most Merciful (al-Rahim) to the believers.

In the heavens and the earth, with its mountains, plains and seas, and in the alternation of night and day, in their lengths and shortness, in darkness and light, and in their succession, each replacing the other, and in the ships that sail the seas, carrying what benefits people, and in what God sends down from the sky of rain-water, by which He gives life to the earth, so that it becomes green and radiant after it had been dry, with no vegetation in it, and in what God has scattered in it of every creature that crawls upon the face of the earth, and in His favour upon you through the turning and directing of the winds, and in the clouds made subservient between the sky and the earth: indeed, in all the aforementioned signs are signs of God's oneness and His magnificent blessings, for a people who use their intellect, who grasp the places of proof and understand His evidences for His oneness and for His sole right to be worshipped.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 165:

Despite these decisive proofs, a group of people take, besides Allah, idols, images and saints (awliya'), whom they make equals to Allah the Exalted, and they give them love, veneration and obedience that are fitting only for Allah alone. The believers are greater in love for Allah than the love of these disbelievers for Allah and their gods, because the believers have sincerely devoted all love to Allah, whereas those others have associated others with Him in love. If only those who wronged themselves by associating partners with Allah in this worldly life knew, when they witness the punishment of the Hereafter, that Allah alone holds all power, and that Allah is severe in punishment, they would not have taken, besides Allah, gods to worship besides Him and to seek nearness to Allah through.

When they witness the punishment of the Hereafter, the leaders who were followed will disown those who followed them into polytheism, and all the bonds that tied them together in the world will be severed: kinship, following, religion, and everything else.

The followers will say: "If only we had a chance to return to the world, so that we could declare our disassociation from these leaders, just as they declared their disassociation from us." Just as Allah shows them the severity of His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, He will show them their false deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never come out of the Fire.

O mankind, eat of what Allah has made lawful and good for you on the earth, which is pure and not impure, beneficial and not harmful. Do not follow the paths of Satan in declaring things lawful and unlawful, or in innovations and acts of disobedience. Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.

Satan only commands you to every evil sin that will harm you, and to every act of disobedience of extreme ugliness, and to attribute falsehood to Allah, such as declaring lawful things unlawful and other things, without knowledge.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 170:

When the believers advise those who are astray, saying: "Follow what Allah has sent down of the Qur'an and guidance," they insist on imitating their idolatrous ancestors, saying: "We will not follow your religion, but we will follow what we found our fathers upon." Would they follow their fathers even though those fathers understood nothing of Allah and did not attain right guidance?

The likeness of those who disbelieve, and of the one who calls them to guidance and faith, is like the likeness of a shepherd who shouts at beasts and drives them, while they do not understand the meanings of his speech, and they only hear the call and the sound of the voice alone. These disbelievers are deaf: they have shut their ears against the truth. They are dumb: they have silenced their tongues from speaking it. They are blind: their eyes do not see its dazzling proofs. So they do not put their minds to use in what would benefit them.

O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you with, and do not be like the disbelievers who forbid the good things and make lawful the foul things. Be thankful to Allah for His great blessings upon you, with your hearts, your tongues and your limbs, if you truly submit to His command, listen and obey Him, and worship Him alone, with no partner.

This is a translation of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex) on Surah 2, verse 173.

Indeed, Allah has forbidden you only what is harmful to you: carrion that was not slaughtered in the lawful manner, flowing blood, the flesh of swine, and animals that were slaughtered for other than Allah. And it is of Allah's bounty and facilitation toward you that He has permitted you to eat these forbidden things in cases of necessity. So whoever is compelled by necessity to eat any of them, without being wrongful in eating more than his need, nor transgressing the bounds of Allah concerning what has been permitted to him, there is no sin upon him in that. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving toward His servants, Merciful to them.

The Noble Qur'an, the Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), on surah 2, verse 174:

Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has revealed in His Books concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and other truths, and who are eager to take a small price in exchange for the goods of this worldly life in return for this concealment, they eat nothing in return for concealing the truth except the Fire of Hell blazing in their bellies. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, due to His anger and wrath against them, and He will not purify them from the defilement of their sins and their disbelief. For them is a painful punishment.

Those who possess these attributes have exchanged misguidance for guidance and the punishment of God for His forgiveness. How bold they are in facing the Fire, by their deeds that are the deeds of the people of the Fire! God marvels at their daring to do this, so marvel, O people, at their boldness and at their endurance of the Fire and their remaining in it. This is said in a manner of contempt for them and of belittling their affair.

That punishment which they deserved is because Allah, exalted is He, sent down His Books to His messengers containing the clear truth, but they disbelieved in it. Indeed, those who differed concerning the Book, believing in part of it and disbelieving in part of it, are in a state of profound discord and division, far from right guidance and correctness.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 177:

It is not righteousness before Allah -exalted is He- to turn one's face in prayer towards the east or the west, if it is not in accordance with Allah's command and His law. Rather, true righteousness is the faith of one who believes in Allah, affirms Him as the sole object of worship with no partner, believes in the Day of Resurrection and recompense, in all the angels, in all the revealed Books, and in all the prophets without making any distinction between them; who gives wealth voluntarily, despite his strong love for it, to close relatives, to orphaned needy children whose fathers have died while they are below the age of maturity (al-baligh), to the poor who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, to needy travellers who are far from their families and their wealth, to beggars who have been compelled to ask because of their severe need, and who spend in freeing slaves and captives; who establishes the prayer and pays the obligatory zakat (zakah); who fulfil their covenants; and who are patient in times of poverty and sickness, and in the heat of battle. Those who possess these qualities are the ones who have been truthful in their faith, and it is they who are the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), who have guarded themselves against Allah's punishment by avoiding His prohibitions.

O you who have believed, Allah and His Messenger, and act according to His law: retaliation (al-qisas) is prescribed for you regarding the murdered, by killing the one who has intentionally killed, on condition of equality and parity: the free man is killed for the free man, whether the man for the woman or the woman for the man, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. Then whoever is pardoned by the guardian of the murdered person, by waiving retaliation against him and being content with taking the blood money (al-diyah), which is a specific amount of wealth that the offender pays in exchange for being pardoned, then both parties should observe good conduct: the guardian should demand the blood money without violence, and the killer should pay him his due graciously, without delay or shortfall. That pardon along with taking the blood money is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy to you, because of the ease and benefit it contains. Whoever kills the killer after pardoning him and accepting the blood money, for him is a painful punishment: he will be killed in retaliation in this world, or [receive] the Fire in the Hereafter.

For you, in the legislation of *qisas* (retaliation in kind) and its implementation, there is a secure life, O people of sound minds, so that you may attain *taqwa* (God-consciousness) of Allah and His fear by always obeying Him.

God has prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, he should make a bequest of a portion of his wealth to his parents and close relatives, observing what is just: so he should not leave the poor and bequeath to the rich, and he should not exceed one-third. This is a binding right, acted upon by those of taqwa (God-consciousness), who fear God. This was before the revelation of the verses of inheritance (al-mawarith), in which God specified the share of each heir.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 181:

So whoever alters the bequest after hearing it from the deceased before his death, the sin is only upon those who alter and change it. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing of your bequests and your statements, All-Knowing of what your hearts conceal of inclination toward truth and justice or toward injustice and deviation, and He will recompense you for that.

Whoever perceives that a testator has deviated from what is right in his bequest, whether by mistake or intentionally, and so advises the testator at the time of the bequest toward what is most equitable, or if that does not come about, then reconciles the parties by altering the bequest so that it conforms to the Sharia, then there is no sin upon him in this reconciliation. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to His servants, Most Merciful to them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: Allah has prescribed fasting for you, just as He prescribed it for the nations before you, so that you may become mindful of your Lord, placing between yourselves and sins a protection through obedience to Him and worship of Him alone.

Allah has prescribed for you the fasting of a number of specified days, and they are the days of the month of Ramadan. Whoever among you is sick, for whom fasting is burdensome, or who is traveling, then he may break the fast, and he must make up a number of other days equal to the days he broke the fast on. As for those who find fasting an unbearable hardship, such as the very old man and the sick person whose recovery is not expected, they must give a ransom (fidyah) for each day they break the fast, which is feeding a needy person who does not own what would suffice him and meet his need. Whoever adds to the amount of the ransom voluntarily, it is better for him. And your fasting is better for you than giving the ransom, if you only knew the great virtue of fasting with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 185:
