The month of Ramadan, in which Allah began sending down the Qur'an on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), as guidance for mankind to the truth; in it are the clearest proofs of Allah's guidance and of the distinction between truth and falsehood. So whoever among you witnesses the month, while being healthy and resident, let him fast its day. The sick and the traveler are permitted to break the fast, and then they make up the same number of days. Allah intends for you ease and facility in His laws, and does not intend for you hardship and difficulty; and that you complete the number of the fast as a month, and that you conclude the fast by glorifying Allah at the Festival of Breaking the Fast (ʿId al-Fitr), and that you magnify Him for His guidance to you, and that you may give thanks to Him for what He has bestowed upon you of guidance, success and facilitation.

And when My servants ask you, O Prophet, concerning Me, [tell them]: I am near. I answer the supplication of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them obey Me in what I have commanded them and forbidden them, and let them believe in Me, that they may be guided to the benefits of their religion and their worldly life. In this verse, God, glorified is He, informs of His nearness to His servants, a nearness befitting His majesty.

Allah has permitted you, on the nights of the month of Ramadan, to have intercourse with your wives. They are a covering for you, and you are a covering for them. Allah knew that you were betraying yourselves by violating what He had forbidden you, namely having intercourse with women after the night prayer ('isha') during the nights of fasting, and this was at the beginning of Islam. So Allah turned to you in forgiveness and eased the matter for you. Now, have intercourse with them and seek what Allah has decreed for you of children. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread of night, by the appearance of true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq). Then complete the fast by abstaining from the things that break it until nightfall, by the setting of the sun.

And do not have intercourse with your wives, or engage in anything that leads to it, while you are in seclusion (i'tikaf) in the mosques, because this invalidates the i'tikaf (which is staying in the mosque for a known period with the intention of drawing near to Allah the Exalted).

These rulings which Allah has prescribed for you are His limits that separate the lawful from the unlawful, so do not approach them, lest you fall into the unlawful. In this clear manner Allah makes His signs and rulings clear to people, so that they may be mindful of Him and fear Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 188:

Do not consume one another's wealth by false means, such as false oaths, usurpation, theft, bribery, usury (riba), and the like. Do not bring your cases before the rulers with false proofs, in order to consume, through litigation, a portion of people's wealth wrongfully, while you know that it is forbidden for you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 189:

Your companions ask you, O Prophet, about the new moons (al-ahilla) and the changes in their phases. Say to them: Allah has made the new moons markers by which people know the times of their acts of worship that are fixed by time, such as fasting and Hajj, and their transactions. Righteousness does not lie in what you were accustomed to in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam) and in the early days of Islam, namely entering houses from their backs when you are in ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah, thinking that this is an act of drawing near to Allah. Rather, righteousness is the deed of one who fears Allah and avoids sins. Enter houses through their doors when you are in ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah, and fear Allah, the Exalted, in all your affairs, so that you may succeed in attaining everything you love of the good of this world and the Hereafter.

Fight in the way of Allah, O believers, to support the religion of Allah against those who fight you, but do not commit the prohibited acts, such as mutilation (al-muthla), misappropriation of war spoils (al-ghulul), and killing those whom it is not permissible to kill, such as women, children, the elderly, and those in their category. Indeed, Allah does not love those who transgress His limits, so they make lawful what Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) have forbidden.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 191:

And kill them wherever you encounter them, among those who fight you from among the polytheists, and expel them from the place from which they expelled you, which is Makkah. And fitnah (trial, persecution; here meaning disbelief, polytheism, and barring people from Islam) is more severe than your killing them. And do not begin fighting them at the Sacred Mosque, out of reverence for its sanctity, until they begin fighting you therein; but if they fight you in the Sacred Mosque, then kill them there. Such is the fitting, deterrent recompense for the disbelievers.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 192:

If they give up the disbelief they are in and their fighting against you near the Sacred Mosque, and enter into faith, then indeed Allah is Forgiving to His servants and Merciful to them.

And continue, O believers, in fighting the aggressive polytheists, until there is no more fitna (persecution that turns people away from their religion) against the Muslims in their religion, and no more shirk (associating partners with God), and religion is for God alone, purely, with none worshipped alongside Him. But if they cease from disbelief and fighting, then cease from them, for punishment is only for those who persist in their disbelief and aggression.

The fighting you (believers) undertake against the polytheists in the sacred month, the month in which Allah has forbidden fighting, is a retribution for their fighting you in the sacred month. Whoever violates what Allah has forbidden, of place and time, shall be requited with the like of his deed and of its kind. So whoever attacks you with fighting or otherwise, inflict upon him a punishment equal to his offence, and there is no blame upon you in that, because it is they who began the aggression. "And fear Allah" – so do not exceed the equivalence in punishment – "and know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him," obeying Him by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden.

And persist, O believers, in spending your wealth to support the religion of Allah, and in striving (jihad) in His cause. Do not cast yourselves into destruction by abandoning jihad in the way of Allah and failing to spend in it. Be excellent in spending and in obedience, and make all your deeds purely for the sake of Allah's countenance. Indeed, Allah loves those who are sincere and excellent in their conduct.

And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for the sake of Allah, sincerely devoted to Him. But if you are prevented from proceeding to complete them after entering into ihram for them, by an impediment such as an enemy or illness, then it is incumbent upon you to sacrifice whatever animal is available to you, of camels, cattle or sheep, drawing near to Allah, so that you may exit your state of ihram by shaving the head or trimming the hair. Do not shave your heads while you are muhsarun (those prevented from completing the rites), until the one who is prevented slaughters his offering at the place where he was prevented, and then exits his ihram, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughtered at al-Hudaybiyah and then shaved his head. Whoever is not prevented may slaughter the offering only in the Haram, which is its place, on the day of Eid — the tenth day — and the days of tashriq after it. So whoever among you is ill, or has an ailment of the head that requires him to shave while he is in ihram, he shall shave, and he must pay a ransom: by fasting three days, or feeding six needy persons, each needy person half a sa' of food, or slaughtering a sheep for the poor of the Haram. When you are in safety and health: whoever enjoys the 'Umrah until the Hajj, that is, by making lawful what was forbidden to him because of ihram after finishing his 'umrah, then he must sacrifice whatever offering is available to him. Whoever does not find an offering to slaughter must fast three days during the months of Hajj, and seven when you have finished the rites of Hajj and returned to your families; those are ten complete days that must be fasted. That offering, and the fasting that follows from it, is for one whose family are not residents of the land of the Haram. Fear Allah, be mindful of carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and know that Allah is severe in punishment toward one who opposes His command and commits what He has forbidden.

The time of Hajj is well-known months: they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. Whoever undertakes the Hajj in them by entering into ihram, then sexual intercourse and its preliminaries, whether by speech or action, are forbidden to him; and it is forbidden to him to leave the obedience of Allah, the Exalted, by committing sins, and to engage in disputing during Hajj that leads to anger and hatred. ﴿And whatever good you do, Allah knows it,﴾ so He will reward each one for his deed. ﴿And take provision for yourselves; but the best provision is righteousness;﴾ provision of food and drink for the journey of Hajj, and provision of righteous deeds for the Hereafter. ﴿And fear Me, O people of sound intellect.﴾

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 198:**

There is no blame on you for seeking bounty from your Lord through profit from trade during the days of Hajj. When you surge forward after sunset, returning from 'Arafat (the place where the pilgrims stand on the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah), then remember Allah with glorification (tasbih), with the talbiyah (the call "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk," meaning "Here I am, O Allah, here I am"), and with supplication at al-Mash'ar al-Haram (Muzdalifah). Remember Allah in the proper manner to which He has guided you, though you were before this guidance among those who had gone astray and did not know the truth.

Let your departure from 'Arafat be the place from which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) departed, differing thereby from those of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) who would not stand there. And ask Allah to forgive your sins. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to His servants who seek forgiveness and repent, and Most Merciful to them.

Then when you have completed your rites and finished the acts of Hajj, remember Allah abundantly and extol Him, as you once remembered the glorious deeds of your forefathers, and even more than that. Among people there is a group whose whole concern is the worldly life alone, so they pray, saying: "Our Lord, grant us good in this world," meaning health, wealth and children. Such people have no share or portion in the Hereafter, because they turn away from it and confine their concern to this world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 201:

Among the people is one who believes and says in his supplication: ﴿Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾ He asks for well-being, provision, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds, and other matters of religion and worldly life in this world, and in the Hereafter Paradise, and that He turn away from us the punishment of the Fire. This supplication is among the most comprehensive of supplications, and for this reason it was most often the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ), as is established in the two Sahihs.

Those who make this supplication will have a great reward, because of the good deeds they have earned. And Allah is swift in reckoning, counting the deeds of His servants and recompensing them for them.

Remember Allah by glorifying Him and proclaiming His greatness during the few numbered days, which are the days of tashriq: the eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Whoever hastens to leave Mina before the sun sets on the twelfth day, after throwing the pebbles (al-jimar), there is no sin upon him; and whoever stays behind by spending the night in Mina until he throws the pebbles on the thirteenth day, there is no sin upon him either, for the one who fears Allah in his pilgrimage. Staying behind is better, because it is an increase in worship and following the example of the Prophet (ﷺ). Fear Allah, O Muslims, and be mindful of Him in all your deeds, and know that you will be gathered to Him alone after your death, for reckoning and recompense.

Among the people there is one who, from the hypocrites, pleases you, O Messenger, with his eloquent speech, which he intends for a share of the worldly goods rather than the Hereafter. He swears by God, calling Him to witness, to what is in his heart of love for Islam, and in this there is the utmost audacity toward God. Yet he is extremely hostile and contentious toward Islam and the Muslims.

When he leaves you, O Messenger, he goes about the earth eagerly and energetically, to spread corruption in it, to destroy people's crops and to kill their livestock. And Allah does not love corruption.

And when this hypocritical corrupter is advised and told, "Fear Allah and beware of His punishment, and cease corrupting the earth," he does not accept the advice; rather, arrogance and the zeal of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic state of ignorance) drive him to further sins. Hell is sufficient for him as a punishment and is enough for him, and what an evil resting-place it is.

And among mankind is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah, by striving in His cause and committing himself to His obedience. And Allah is Kind (Ra'uf) to His servants; He shows great mercy to His believing servants, in this world and in the Hereafter, and so He rewards them with the best of rewards.

O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, and in Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and in Islam as religion: enter into all of the laws of Islam, acting upon all of its rulings, and do not leave aside any part of them. And do not follow the paths of Satan in what he calls you to of acts of disobedience. Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you, so beware of him.

If you deviate from the path of truth after clear proofs have come to you from the Qur'an and the Sunnah, then know that Allah is Almighty in His dominion, nothing escapes Him, and He is Wise in His command and His prohibition, placing everything in its proper place.

What are these stubborn disbelievers waiting for, after the clear proofs have been established, other than that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, should come to them in a manner befitting Him, subhanahu, amid canopies of clouds on the Day of Resurrection, so that He may judge between them with just judgment; and that the angels should come. At that time Allah, exalted is He, will pass His judgment upon them. And to Him alone are returned the affairs of all creation.

Ask, O Messenger, the Children of Israel who oppose you: how many clear signs did We give them in their scriptures, guiding them to the truth? Yet they disbelieved in all of them, turned away from them, and distorted them from their proper places. And whoever exchanges the blessing of God, which is His religion, and disbelieves in it after knowing it and after the proof has been established against him through it, then indeed God is severe in punishment for him.

The Glorious Qur'an was revealed in a context where the Makkan disbelievers mocked the believers. Here is the commentary on the verse.

Made attractive to those who denied the Oneness of Allah is the worldly life and what it contains of desires and pleasures, and they mock the believers. But those who fear their Lord will be above all the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, where Allah will admit them to the highest ranks of Paradise, and He will cast the disbelievers to the lowest levels of the Fire. And Allah provides for whomever He wills of His creation without reckoning.

The people were one community, agreed upon belief in God; then they differed in their religion. So God sent the prophets as callers to the religion of God, giving good news of Paradise to whoever obeyed God, and warning whoever disbelieved in Him and disobeyed Him of the Fire. He sent down with them the heavenly Books containing the truth they held, so that they might judge among people by what was in them concerning what they differed over. None differed about the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Book out of injustice and envy except those to whom God gave the Torah and who knew what it contained of proofs and rulings. So God, by His grace, guided the believers to distinguish truth from falsehood and to know what they had differed over. And God guides whomever He wills of His servants to a straight path.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 214:

Do you think, O believers, that you will enter Paradise while you have not yet been afflicted with trials like those that befell the believers who passed away before you: poverty, sicknesses, fear and terror. They were shaken with all kinds of frightening things, until their messenger and the believers with him said, out of haste for victory from Allah, the Exalted: "When will the victory of Allah come?" Surely, the victory of Allah is near to the believers.

The Noble Qur'an Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 215:

They ask you, O Prophet, what they should spend from the various kinds of their wealth seeking nearness to Allah, and upon whom they should spend. Say to them: Spend whatever good is within your means from the various kinds of lawful and good wealth, and direct your spending to parents, to the nearest relatives from among your family and kin, to orphans whose fathers have died while they are below the age of puberty, to the needy who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, and to the traveler in need who is far from his family and his wealth. And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is All-Knowing of it.

God has enjoined upon you, O believers, fighting against the disbelievers. Fighting is disliked by you by nature, because of its hardship and its many dangers. You may dislike something that is in reality good for you, and you may love something that, because of the ease or immediate pleasure it brings, is in fact bad for you. God, exalted is He, knows what is good for you, while you do not know that. So hasten to jihad in His cause.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 217:

They ask you, O Messenger, about the sacred month: is fighting in it permitted? Say to them: fighting in the sacred month is a grave matter in the sight of Allah, but barring people from the path of Allah, disbelieving in Him, His Messenger and His religion, preventing the Muslims from entering the Sacred Mosque, and expelling the Prophet and the Muhajirun from it, though they are its people and its protectors, is a greater sin and a more serious offence in the sight of Allah than fighting in the sacred month. Shirk, in which you are engaged, is greater and more severe than killing in the sacred month. These disbelievers have not desisted from their crimes; rather, they persist in them, and they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion to disbelief, if they are able to achieve that. Whoever among you, O Muslims, obeys them and apostatises from his religion and dies in disbelief, his deeds will have been lost in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be among the companions of the Fire, abiding in it forever.

This is a translation of the commentary text (a tafsir passage) on Qur'an 2:218.

The commentary text is: "Indeed, those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and have acted in accordance with His law, and those who emigrated from their homelands and strove in the way of Allah, those hope for the bounty and reward of Allah. And Allah is All-Forgiving toward the sins of His believing servants, and Most Merciful to them with vast mercy."

The Muyassar (Commentary of King Fahd Complex) on surah 2, verse 219:

They ask you, O Prophet, about the ruling on consuming intoxicants (khamr), whether by drinking, selling, or buying. Khamr is every intoxicant that overtakes the intellect and covers it, whether it is a drink or something eaten. And they ask you about the ruling on gambling (qimar), which is taking or giving wealth through gambling, that is, contests of chance in which there is a return from both parties. Say to them: in these two there are many harms and corruptions, in matters of religion and worldly life, of the intellect and of wealth. And in them there are benefits for people in terms of earning wealth and other things, but their sin is greater than their benefit, since they turn people away from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer, and they cause enmity and hatred among people, and they waste wealth. This was a preparation for their prohibition. And they ask you about the amount that they spend from their wealth as voluntary charity and alms. Say to them: spend the amount that exceeds your needs. Thus Allah makes clear to you the signs and the rulings of the Sharia, so that you may reflect on what benefits you in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 220:

"They ask you, O Prophet, about orphans: how should they conduct themselves toward them regarding their livelihood and their wealth?" Say to them: "Your setting things right for them is good. So always do what is most beneficial for them. And if you mix with them in all matters of livelihood, they are your brothers in religion. A brother must look after his brother's interests. Allah knows the one who wastes orphans' wealth from the one who is keen to set it right. Had Allah willed, He would have made things narrow and difficult for you by forbidding mixing with them. Indeed Allah is Almighty in His dominion, Wise in His creation, His management and His legislation."

Do not marry idolatrous women, O Muslims, until they enter Islam. Know that a slave woman who has no wealth and no lineage, but who believes in God, is better than an idolatrous woman, even if the free idolatress pleases you. And do not marry your believing women, whether slave girls or free women, to idolaters until they believe in God and His Messenger. Know that a believing slave, despite his poverty, is better than an idolater, even if the idolater pleases you. Those who are characterized by polytheism, men and women, invite everyone who associates with them to that which leads them to the Fire, while God, glorified is He, invites His servants to His true religion, which leads them to Paradise and the forgiveness of their sins by His permission, and He makes His signs and rulings clear to people so that they may take heed and be admonished.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 222:

They ask you about menstruation (al-ḥayd), which is the blood that flows from women's wombs naturally at specific times. Say, [O Prophet]: it is a harmful impurity that harms whoever approaches it. So keep away from intercourse with women during the period of menstruation until the blood stops. When the blood has stopped and they have performed ghusl (ritual bath), then have intercourse with them in the place which Allah has permitted for you, that is the front passage (al-qubul), not the back passage (al-dubur). Indeed, Allah loves His servants who often seek forgiveness and repent, and He loves His servants who purify themselves, who keep away from immoral acts and filth.

Your wives are a tilth for you (a place of sowing), so you may approach your tilth however you wish, but you sow the seed in their wombs, and children come forth from it by the will of Allah. So have intercourse with them only in the place of intercourse, which is the front passage (al-qubul), in whatever manner you wish. And send forth good deeds for yourselves by observing the commands of Allah. Fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him for reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. And give good news, O Prophet, to the believers, of that which will gladden and delight them: the good recompense in the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 224:

And do not make your oaths by Allah, O Muslims, a barrier preventing you from righteousness, maintaining ties of kinship, piety, and reconciliation between people, such that when you are called upon to do any of these, you argue that you had sworn by Allah not to do it. Rather, the one who has taken an oath should turn away from his oath, do acts of righteousness, expiate for his oath, and not make a habit of it. And Allah is All-Hearing of your statements, All-Knowing of all your circumstances.

Allah will not hold you accountable for your oaths that you swear without intention, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have intended. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving to whoever turns back to Him in repentance, Most Forbearing with whoever disobeys Him, since He does not hasten to punish him.

For those who swear not to have intercourse with their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they return to them before the four months have passed, then Allah is Forgiving toward what they uttered of the oath, because of their return, and Merciful to them.

And if they resolve upon divorce, by persisting in their oath and abstaining from intercourse, then indeed Allah is All-Hearing of their words and All-Knowing of their intentions, and He will recompense them for that.

The divorced women who menstruate must wait, without remarrying, for a period of three purity-periods or three menstrual cycles as a waiting period ('iddah), so that they may be certain their wombs are free of pregnancy. It is not permissible for them to marry another man during this waiting period until it ends. It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, of pregnancy or menstruation, if the divorced women truly believe in Allah and the Last Day. The husbands of the divorced women have more right to take them back during the waiting period. This should be with the intention of reconciliation and good, not with the intention of harm, by torturing them through prolonging the waiting period. Women have rights over men comparable to the duties men have toward them, in accordance with what is known as good, and men have a degree above them in good companionship, kind association, guardianship over the household, and possession of divorce. Allah is Almighty, with overpowering might, and All-Wise, who places everything in its appropriate position.

The divorce that permits return (to the wife) is twice, one after the other. So God's ruling after each pronouncement is either to keep the woman honorably, treating her well in marriage after taking her back, or to release her with good treatment by fulfilling her rights, and that her divorcer should not mention her with harm. It is not lawful for you, O husbands, to take back anything of what you have given them of the bridal gift (mahr) and the like, except when the spouses fear that they will not uphold the marital rights. In that case, they bring their matter before the guardians (awliya'). If the guardians fear that the spouses will not keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame on the spouses regarding what the woman gives the husband in exchange for her divorce (khul'). Those rulings are the limits of God that separate the lawful from the unlawful, so do not transgress them. Whoever transgresses the limits of God, the Exalted, those are the wrongdoers against themselves by exposing themselves to the punishment of God.

If a man divorces his wife with the third pronouncement, then she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband in a valid marriage and he has consummated it with her, and the marriage must be out of genuine desire, not with the intention of making her lawful to her first husband. If the second husband divorces her, or dies leaving her, and her waiting period ('iddah) has ended, then there is no sin upon the woman and her first husband in their returning to each other with a new contract and a new bridal gift (mahr), if they believe that they will uphold the limits of Allah which He has prescribed for spouses. And these are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear for a people who have knowledge of His commands and limits, for they are the ones who benefit from them.

When you divorce women and they approach the end of their waiting period, then either take them back with the intention of treating them well in a manner that is good by the standards of the Sharia and of custom, or let them go until their waiting period ends. Beware of taking them back with the intent of harming them, in order to transgress against their rights. Whoever does that has wronged himself by making himself deserving of punishment. Do not take the signs and rulings of Allah in jest and frivolity. Remember Allah's blessing upon you in Islam and in the detailed explanation of the rulings. Remember what Allah has sent down to you of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and thank Him, glorified is He, for these great blessings. Allah reminds you of this and warns you against opposing it, so fear Allah and watch over Him. Know that Allah is all-knowing of everything; nothing is hidden from Him, and He will recompense each person according to what they deserve.

When you divorce your wives with fewer than three pronouncements, and their waiting period ends without your taking them back, then do not hinder them, O guardians, from remarrying their former husbands by a new contract if they wish that and mutual consent has been established in accordance with the Sharia and custom. This is what whoever among you believes truly in God and the Last Day is admonished with. Leaving off obstruction (al-'adl) and enabling the husbands to marry their wives again is more conducive to growth and purity for your honour, and of greater benefit and reward for you. God knows what is good for you, and you do not know that.

And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing period. It is obligatory upon the fathers to provide for the divorced nursing mothers their food and clothing, in the manner that is commendable according to the Shariah and custom, because Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. It is not permissible for the parents to make the infant a means of harm between them. It is obligatory upon the heir, upon the death of the father, to provide the same maintenance and clothing that the father was obligated to provide before his death. If the two parents wish to wean the infant before the end of the two years, there is no blame upon them if they both agree and consult together about that, so that they reach what is in the infant's interest. And if the two parents agree to have the infant nursed by another wet nurse other than its mother, there is no blame upon them, provided the father gives the mother her due and gives the wet nurse her wage in accordance with what people customarily agree upon. And fear Allah in all your circumstances, and know that Allah is All-Seeing of what you do, and He will recompense you for that.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 2, verse 234:

"Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they must wait by themselves for a period of four months and ten days. They should not leave the marital home, nor adorn themselves, nor remarry. When the stated period has ended, there is no blame upon you, O guardians of the women, for what they do with themselves of going out, adorning themselves, and marrying in the manner prescribed by the Shariah. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is All-Aware of your deeds, outward and inward, and He will recompense you for them."

There is no sin upon you, O men, for what you hint at of proposing marriage to women whose husbands have died or who have been irrevocably divorced during their waiting period. Nor is there any blame upon you for what you conceal within yourselves of intention to marry them after their waiting period ends. God knows that you will mention the women in waiting, and you will not be patient enough to refrain from speaking of them, out of your weakness; therefore He has permitted you to mention them by allusion or to harbour the intention within yourselves. But beware of making them promises of marriage in secret, such as illicit intercourse, or agreeing upon a marriage during the waiting period, except that you say a saying that conveys that such a woman is desired by husbands. And do not resolve upon concluding the marriage contract during the time of the waiting period until its term has ended. Know that God knows what is within yourselves, so fear Him. And know that God is Forgiving to whoever repents from his sins, Forbearing toward His servants, not hastening to punish them.

There is no blame upon you, O husbands, if you divorce women after contracting marriage with them and before you have touched them, or before you have specified a dower for them. And provide for them with something from which they may benefit, to console them and to ease the distress of divorce, and to remove resentment. This provision is due according to the circumstances of the divorcing man: upon the wealthy according to the extent of his means, and upon the poor according to what he possesses, as a provision in a manner recognized by the Sharia, and it is a right established upon those who do good to the divorced women and to themselves through obedience to God.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 237:

And if you divorce women after contracting marriage with them, but before you have had intercourse with them, yet you have bound yourselves to a specified dower for them, then it is obligatory upon you to give them half of the agreed dower, unless the divorced women forgo it, leaving aside the half of the dower due to them, or the husband allows the divorced woman to keep the whole dower. Your forgoing, O men and women, is closer to fearing Allah and obeying Him. And do not forget, O people, the bounty and benevolence among you, which is giving what is not obligatory upon you, and forgiveness in rights. Indeed Allah is All-Seeing of what you do. He encourages you towards what is good and urges you to show generosity.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 238:

O Muslims, maintain the five obligatory prayers by performing them regularly at their appointed times, with their conditions, pillars and obligations. Maintain also the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta), which is the Asr prayer, and stand in your prayer obedient to Allah, humbly submissive and lowly before Him.

If you fear an enemy, then pray while walking or riding, in whatever manner you are able, even by gesturing, or facing a direction other than the qiblah. Then, when your fear has passed, perform the prayer of safety, remember God in it, and do not reduce it from its original form. And give thanks to Him for teaching you matters of worship and rulings that you did not know before.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 240:

And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, let them make a bequest for their wives: that they be provided for (yumatta'na) a full year from the day of death, by residing in the husband's house without the heirs evicting them during the year, as a way of consoling the wife and showing kindness to the deceased. But if the wives leave of their own choice before the year is over, then there is no sin upon you, O heirs, in that, nor is there any blame upon the wives for what they do with themselves of lawful matters. And Allah is Mighty in His dominion, Wise in His command and His prohibition. This verse has been abrogated (mansukh) by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind them shall wait with themselves four months and ten days﴾.

For divorced women there is provision (متاع) of clothing and maintenance in a fair manner, as is known and approved by the Sharia, as a duty upon those who fear Allah and guard themselves against His command and prohibition.

Such is the clear explanation regarding the rulings on children and women: Allah makes His verses and rulings clear to you in everything you need for your livelihood and your afterlife, so that you may understand them and act upon them.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the story of those who fled from their homes and dwellings, and they were many thousands, fearing death from plague or from fighting? So God said to them: "Die," and they died all at once, as a punishment for their fleeing from the decree of God. Then God revived them after a while, so that they might complete their appointed terms, take warning, and repent. Indeed, God is possessed of great bounty toward mankind through His many blessings, but most people do not give thanks for God's favor upon them.
And fight, O Muslims, the disbelievers in support of the religion of Allah. Know that Allah is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your intentions and your deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 245:

Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, out of sincere hope for reward, so that He may multiply it for him many times over, in countless measures of reward and excellent recompense? Allah restricts and expands (provision), so spend and do not fear [want]; for He is the All-Provider. He restricts provision for whom He wills of His servants and expands it for others; He has perfect wisdom in that. And to Him alone you will return after death, and He will recompense you for your deeds.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the story of the eminent and notables of the Children of Israel after the time of Moses? When they asked their prophet to appoint for them a king, under whose leadership they would unite and fight their enemies in the cause of God. Their prophet said to them: "Is it likely, if fighting in the cause of God is prescribed for you, that you will not fight?" That is, I expect that you will be cowardly and flee from battle. They said, marveling at their prophet's expectation: "And what prevents us from fighting in the cause of God, when our enemy has expelled us from our homes and separated us from our children through killing and captivity?" But when God prescribed fighting for them with the king He had appointed for them, they became cowardly and fled from battle, except for a few of them who stood firm by the grace of God. And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers who break their covenants.

Their prophet said to them: "Indeed, Allah has sent Talut (Saul) to you as king, in response to your request. He will lead you to fight your enemy, as you asked."

The leaders of the Children of Israel said: "How can Talut be king over us, when he does not deserve it? For he is not from the tribe of kings, nor from the house of prophethood, and he was not given abundant wealth with which to strengthen his kingship. So we have more right to the kingship than he, because we are from the tribe of kings and from the house of prophethood."

Their prophet said to them: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you, and He, glorified is He, knows best the affairs of His servants. He has increased him in breadth of knowledge and strength of body so that he may strive against the enemy. Allah is the Owner of all sovereignty; He gives His kingship to whomever He wills of His servants. Allah is All-Encompassing in bounty and giving, All-Knowing of the realities of affairs; nothing is hidden from Him."

Their prophet said to them: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, in which is the Torah, and which their enemies had seized from them. In it is tranquility from your Lord that will steady the hearts of the sincere, and in it are remnants of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, such as the staff and the fragments of the tablets, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a greatest proof for you of the choice of Talut as king over you by the command of God, if you are believers in God and His messengers."

Then, when Talut set out with his troops to fight the Amalekites, he said to them: "Indeed, Allah will test you with patience at a river before you that you must cross, so that the believer may be distinguished from the hypocrite. Whoever among you drinks from the river's water is not of my people, and is not fit to fight alongside me. Whoever does not taste the water is of my people, for he obeys my command and is fit for jihad, except for one who takes a dispensation and scoops up a single handful with his hand; there is no blame on him."

When they reached the river, they bent down over the water and drank excessively from it, except for a small number of them who endured the thirst and the heat and were content with a single handful. At that point, the disobedient ones fell behind. When Talut crossed the river, together with the small band of believers who were with him, numbering three hundred and some-odd men, to meet the enemy, and they saw the multitude of their enemy and its numbers, they said: "We have no power today against Jalut and his mighty troops." But those who were certain that they would meet Allah answered, reminding their brethren of Allah and His power, saying: "How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission and command of Allah! Allah is with the patient, by His success, His help, and His good reward."

When they came out against Jalut (Goliath) and his troops and saw the danger with their own eyes, they turned to God in supplication and humble entreaty, saying: "Our Lord, pour out upon us great patience, make our feet firm, and let them stand steadfast in fighting the enemy, not fleeing from the terror of war, and give us victory, by Your help and support, over the disbelieving people."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 251:

﴿فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾. So they routed them by the permission of Allah. David (peace be upon him) killed Goliath (Jalut), the commander of the tyrants, and afterwards Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave David kingship and prophethood among the Children of Israel, and taught him of whatever knowledge He willed.

﴿وَلَوْلَا أَن يَدْفَعُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ﴾. And were it not that Allah repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, by the dominance of disbelief and the entrenchment of tyranny and of the people of sin, where some of the people are those who obey Him and believe in Him, and others are those who disobey Allah and associate partners with Him. ﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. But Allah is full of bounty toward all creatures.
Those are the proofs and evidences of Allah. We recite them to you, O Prophet, with truth, and you are certainly one of the messengers who spoke the truth (ﷺ).

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 253:

These noble messengers: Allah gave some of them preference over others, according to what Allah bestowed upon them. Among them are those whom Allah spoke to directly, such as Musa (Moses) and Muhammad, upon both of them be peace, and in this is an affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the manner befitting His majesty. Among them is the one whom Allah raised to lofty ranks, such as Muhammad (ﷺ), by the universality of his message, the sealing of prophethood with him, the preference of his community over all other nations, and other things. Allah, Exalted is He, gave Isa (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary), upon him be peace, clear signs, dazzling miracles, such as healing the one born blind and the one afflicted with leprosy by Allah's permission, and raising the dead by Allah's permission, and He strengthened him with Jibril (Gabriel), upon him be peace. Had Allah willed that those who came after these messengers would not fight one another, after the clear signs had come to them, they would not have fought. But differences arose among them: some of them remained steadfast in their faith, and some of them persisted in their disbelief. Had Allah willed, after the differences that necessitate fighting had arisen among them, they would not have fought. But Allah grants success to whomever He wills to obey Him and believe in Him, and forsakes whomever He wills, so he disobeys Him and disbelieves in Him. He does what He wills and chooses.

O you who have believed in God, believed in His Messenger, and acted upon his guidance: give out the obligatory zakat, and spend in charity from what God has bestowed upon you, before the Day of Resurrection comes, a Day on which there is no trade that would yield profit, no ransom by which you could redeem yourselves from the punishment of God, no friendship of a friend that could rescue you, and no intercessor who has the power to lighten the punishment for you. And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers who transgress the limits of God.

Allah is He besides whom none deserves to be worshipped or served. Al-Hayy (the Ever-Living), who possesses all the meanings of perfect life as befits His majesty. Al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer of all things). ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾, that is, slumber or sleep. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾; it is all His possession. No one dares to intercede with Him except by His permission. His knowledge encompasses all creatures, past, present and future. He knows what lies before the creatures of the future matters, and what lies behind them of past matters. None of the creation grasps anything of His knowledge except what Allah has taught them and made them aware of. ﴿His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth﴾. The Kursi (the Footstool) is the place of the feet of the Lord, exalted is His majesty, and none knows its reality except Allah, glorified is He. ﴿And He is not burdened by their preservation﴾, glorified is He. He is Al-Ali (the Most High) in His essence and His attributes, above all His creatures, and He combines all the attributes of greatness and grandeur. This verse is the greatest verse in the Qur'an, and it is called (Ayat al-Kursi) (the Verse of the Throne).

Because this religion is complete and its signs are clear, there is no need to compel anyone to accept it, for the proofs are evident, by which truth is distinguished from falsehood, and guidance from error. Whoever disbelieves in everything that is worshipped besides Allah and believes in Allah has held firm and stood upon the best path, and has grasped from the religion the strongest handhold, which never breaks. And Allah is All-Hearing of His servants' statements, All-Knowing of their intentions and deeds, and He will recompense them for that.

God (Allah) is the Guardian (walī) of the believers: He supports them with His help, grants them success, and protects them. He brings them out of the darkness of disbelief (kufr) into the light of faith (īmān). As for those who disbelieve, their helpers and guardians are the equals (andād) and idols (awthān) that they worship besides Allah. They bring them out of the light of faith into the darkness of disbelief. Those are the companions of the Fire, who abide in it constantly, remaining in it forever; they will never come out of it.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the strange case of the one who argued with Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the Oneness of Allah and His Lordship? Allah had given him kingship, so he became arrogant and asked Ibrahim: "Who is your Lord?" Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: "My Lord is the One who gives life to creatures so they live, and takes life from them so they die," meaning that He alone has the power to give life and cause death. He (the king) said: "I give life and cause death," meaning: I kill whomever I wish to kill, and I spare whomever I wish to spare. So Ibrahim said to him: "Indeed, Allah, whom I worship, brings the sun from the east, so can you change this divine law by making it rise from the west?" Thus this disbeliever was bewildered and his argument was cut off, for he is like the wrongdoers, whom Allah does not guide to the truth and the right course.

Or have you (O Messenger) considered the likes of the one who passed by a town whose houses had collapsed, its roofs fallen in upon their foundations, and he said: "How will Allah bring this town back to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then restored his spirit to him and said to him: "How long have you remained [dead]?" He said: "I have remained a day, or part of a day." So He informed him that he had remained dead for a hundred years. He commanded him to look at his food and drink, and at how Allah had preserved them from change over this long period. He commanded him to look at his donkey, how Allah had brought it back to life after it had become scattered bones. And He said to him: ﴿And We will make you a sign for the people﴾, that is, a clear proof of Allah's power to resurrect after death. He commanded him to look at the bones, how Allah raises some of them upon others and joins some of them to others, then clothes them with flesh after they have come together, then returns life into them. When this became clear to him by direct observation, he acknowledged the greatness of Allah, and that He is over all things Powerful, and he became a sign for the people.

Remember, O Messenger, when Abraham asked his Lord to show him how He brings the dead to life. God said to him: ﴿Do you not believe?﴾ He said: "Yes, but I ask this so that my heart may be further assured." He said: ﴿Take four birds and make them incline toward you, then cut them into pieces and place a portion of them on every hill, then call them; they will come to you swiftly.﴾ So Abraham called out, and immediately every piece returned to its place, and behold, the birds came to him swiftly. And know that God is Mighty, nothing overpowers Him, and He is Wise in His sayings, His actions, His legislation, and His decree.

The greatest of the things from which believers benefit is spending in the way of Allah. The likeness of the believers who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that has sprouted in fertile soil: it has produced a stalk from which seven shoots branch out, each bearing an ear, and in each ear there are a hundred grains. Allah multiplies the reward for whomever He wills, according to the faith and perfect sincerity that exist in the heart of the one who spends. The bounty of Allah is vast, and He, glorified is He, is All-Knowing of who deserves it, and is aware of the intentions of His servants.

Those who spend their wealth in the cause of jihad and in various kinds of good, and then do not follow up what they have spent with reminders of their favor (mann) upon those they gave to, nor with harm (adha) by word or deed that makes the recipient feel they have been favored, will have their great reward with their Lord. They will have no fear regarding what they face of the affairs of the Hereafter, nor will they grieve over anything that escaped them in this world.

A kind word and forgiveness of whatever harshness came from the beggar in his insistence are better than a charity followed by harm and injury from the giver. God is free of need from the charity of His servants, and forbearing, not hastening to punish them.

O you who have believed in Allah and the Last Day, do not nullify your charity with reminders of your generosity or harm, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and praised for it, while he does not believe in Allah or affirm the Last Day. The example of such a person is that of a smooth rock covered with earth, upon which a heavy rain falls and washes the earth away, leaving it bare and smooth with nothing on it. Likewise, those who show off will have their deeds come to nothing with Allah, and they will not find any reward for what they spent. And Allah does not guide the disbelievers to what is right in their spending or in anything else.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 265:

And the likeness of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and with a firm conviction in the truth of His promise is like a great garden on a high and fertile ground, upon which heavy rain has fallen, so its fruits are doubled. And if heavy rain does not fall upon it, then a light drizzle suffices for it to yield its doubled fruit. Likewise, the expenditure of the sincere is accepted by Allah and multiplied, whether it is little or much. Allah, who is aware of hidden secrets and sees outward and inward matters, rewards each person according to his sincerity.

Would any one of you wish to have a garden of date palms and grapevines, with rivers of fresh water flowing beneath its trees, and in which he has every kind of fruit, while he has reached old age and cannot plant the like of it, and he has young children who need this garden? Then a fierce wind strikes it, carrying scorching fire, and it is burned up. Thus is the state of those who do not sincerely intend their spending: they come on the Day of Resurrection with no good deeds to their credit. In this way Allah makes clear to you the signs that benefit you, so that you may reflect and make your spending purely for Allah.

O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth, and do not aim for the bad part of it to give away, when you yourselves would not take it except by overlooking what is in it of inferiority and deficiency. So how can you be content to give to God what you would not be content with for yourselves? And know that God, who has provided for you, is free of need from your charity, worthy of praise, praised in every state.

This avarice and choosing the inferior for charity come from Satan, who frightens you with poverty, entices you to be stingy, and commands you to commit sins and disobey God, Exalted is He. Meanwhile, God, glory be to Him, promises you, in return for your spending, forgiveness of your sins and abundant provision. God is All-Encompassing in bounty, All-Knowing of intentions and deeds.

God grants insight into speech and action to whomever He wills of His servants, and whoever is granted this by God has been given abundant good. None takes heed of this and benefits from it except people of sound minds, illuminated by the light and guidance of God.

Whatever you spend, whether of wealth or of something else, be it little or much, seeking the pleasure of Allah, or whatever you vow upon yourselves of wealth or of something else, Allah knows it. He is the One who is aware of your intentions, and He will reward you for that. And whoever withholds the right of Allah is a wrongdoer, and the wrongdoers have no helpers who could protect them from the punishment of Allah.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 271:

If you make your charity public, it is good; but if you give it secretly and hand it to the poor, that is better for you, because it is further from showing off. In charity, together with sincerity, there is an erasing of your sins. And Allah, who knows the finest details of matters, nothing of your circumstances is hidden from Him, and He will reward each person according to his deeds.

You, O Messenger, are not responsible for guiding the disbelievers to right guidance; rather, God expands the breast of whomever He wills for His religion, and grants them success in it. Whatever good you spend of wealth will return its benefit to you from God, and the believers spend only seeking the pleasure of God. Whatever you spend of wealth, sincerely for God, you will be given its reward in full, and you will not be wronged in any of it. In the verse is an affirmation of the attribute of the Face for God, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting Him.

Give your charity to the poor among the Muslims who are unable to travel in search of provision, because they are occupied with jihad in the way of Allah. Someone who does not know them thinks they are not in need of charity, because of their restraint from asking. You recognise them by their marks and the traces of need upon them. They do not ask people at all, and if they are compelled to ask, they do not press their request. And whatever wealth you spend in the way of Allah, nothing of it is hidden from Allah, and He will reward it with the fullest and most complete reward on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 274:

Those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah, by night and by day, secretly and openly, will have their reward with their Lord. There shall be no fear for them regarding what they will face of the matters of the Hereafter, nor shall they grieve over what they have missed of the portions of this world. That wise divine legislation is the method of Islam in spending, for in it is the meeting of the needs of the poor with dignity and honour, the purification of the wealth of the rich, and the realisation of cooperation in righteousness and piety, seeking the Face of Allah, without coercion or compulsion.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 275:**

Those who consume interest (al-riba, which is the excess over the principal) will not rise from their graves on the Day of Resurrection except as one rises whom Satan has driven mad by his touch. That is because they said: "Trade is only like interest," in that both are permissible and both lead to an increase in wealth. So Allah refuted them and made clear that He has permitted trade and forbidden interest, because trade and buying and selling bring benefit to individuals and communities, while interest brings exploitation, loss and ruin. Whoever receives the prohibition of Allah concerning interest and refrains from it, then what he has already gained before the prohibition reached him is his, and he bears no sin for it, and his affair is with Allah regarding what remains of his life. If he persists in his repentance, then Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers. But whoever returns to interest after the prohibition of Allah has reached him, he has deserved the punishment, and the proof has been established against him. For this reason He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

God destroys interest (riba) entirely, or deprives its practitioner of the blessing in his wealth, so that he gains no benefit from it. And He causes charity (sadaqat) to grow and multiply, multiplies the reward for those who give in charity, and blesses their wealth for them. And Allah does not love every person who persists in disbelief, who considers the consumption of interest lawful, and who persists in sin, what is unlawful, and acts of disobedience to Allah.

Indeed, those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, do righteous deeds, establish the prayer as Allah and His Messenger commanded, and pay the zakat on their wealth, will have a great reward specific to them with their Lord, who is their Provider. No fear will befall them in their Hereafter, and they will not grieve over the portions of their worldly life that they have missed.

O you who have believed in Allah and followed His Messenger, fear Allah, and give up seeking whatever remains due to you of additional interest over your capital that was yours before the prohibition of riba, if you are truly affirming your faith in word and deed.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 279:

If you do not desist from what Allah has forbidden you, then be certain of a war from Allah and His Messenger. But if you turn back to your Lord and give up consuming interest (ribā), then you are entitled to the principal of your debts, without any increase: you shall not wrong anyone by taking more than your capital, and no one shall wrong you by reducing what you have lent.

If the debtor is unable to repay, then grant him respite until Allah makes his means easy. But if you forgive it, giving up the principal entirely or in part, that is better for you, if you only knew its merit and that it is better for you in this world and the Hereafter.

Beware, O people, of a Day on which you will be returned to Allah, which is the Day of Resurrection, when you will be presented before Allah to be called to account. He will then recompense each one of you for what he did, whether good or evil, without being wronged. The verse also indicates that abstaining from what Allah has forbidden of riba-based gains completes faith and its obligations, including establishing the prayer, paying the zakat, and doing righteous deeds.

O you who have believed in Allah and followed His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): when you deal with one another in debt for a specified term, write it down, to preserve the wealth and to prevent dispute. Let a trustworthy, competent scribe do the writing between you, and let no one whom Allah has taught writing refuse to do so. Let the debtor dictate what he owes, let him fear his Lord, and let him not diminish anything of the debt. If the debtor is one who cannot manage his property well, or is a minor or insane, or is unable to speak, whether by muteness or by a complete inability to speak, then let the guardian who manages his affairs dictate on his behalf. Call upon two Muslim men, of age and sound mind, who are known for uprightness. If two men cannot be found, then call upon one man and two women whose testimony you find acceptable, so that if one of the two women forgets, the other may remind her. The witnesses must respond to whoever calls them to testify, and they must give their testimony when they are called to it. Do not be weary of writing down the debt, whether it is small or large, up to its specified term. That is more just in the sight of Allah's law and guidance, more effective in establishing and giving testimony, and closer to removing doubt about the kind of debt, its amount, and its term. However, if the matter is one of buying and selling, where you take goods and pay the price on the spot, then there is no need to write it down, though it is recommended to call witnesses to it, to prevent dispute and discord. It is obligatory upon the witness and the scribe to render the testimony and the writing as it should be, as Allah has commanded. It is not permissible for the one who holds the right, or the one who owes it, to harm the scribes and the witnesses, and likewise it is not permissible for the scribes and witnesses to harm those who need their writing or testimony. If you do what you have been forbidden, then it is a departure from the obedience of Allah, and its consequence will befall you. Fear Allah in all that He has commanded you and forbidden you, and Allah will teach you all that sets right your worldly life and your hereafter. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything; nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 2, verse 283:

If you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe to write the debt down for you, then take a pledge in hand (rahn) from the creditor's side: give to the one owed a right something that will serve as a guarantee for his right until the debtor returns what he owes of debt. If some of you trust one another, then there is no blame on you for leaving off writing, calling witnesses, and taking a pledge. The debt remains a trust (amanah) upon the debtor, who must pay it, and who must be mindful of Allah and not betray his creditor. If the debtor denies the debt he owes, and there was someone present who witnessed it, then he must give his testimony, and whoever conceals this testimony is a person of a treacherous, sinful heart. Allah is the One who knows the secrets, whose knowledge encompasses all your affairs, and He will hold you accountable for that.

To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in ownership, in management and in encompassing power, and nothing is hidden from Him. Whether you reveal what is in your souls or conceal it, God knows it, and He will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. God has power over all things. Then God honoured the Muslims after this: He pardoned them for the whispers of the self (ḥadīth al-nafs) and the passing thoughts of the heart, as long as they are not followed by speech or action, as this was established from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ), affirmed and was certain of what was revealed to him from his Lord, and it was right that he should be certain. The believers likewise affirmed and acted upon the Mighty Qur'an. Each of them affirmed that Allah is their Lord and their God, endowed with the attributes of majesty and perfection; that Allah has noble angels; that He sent down Books; and that He sent Messengers to His creation. We believers do not distinguish between any of His Messengers, accepting some and rejecting others; rather, we believe in all of them. The Messenger and the believers said: "We hear, our Lord, what You have revealed, and we obey in all of it. We hope that You will forgive us our sins by Your grace, for You are the One who has nurtured us with the blessings You have bestowed upon us, and to You alone is our return and our final destination."

The religion of God is ease, with no hardship in it. God does not require of His servants what they cannot bear. Whoever does good receives good, and whoever does evil receives evil.

"Our Lord, do not punish us if we forget something You have obligated upon us, or if we err in doing something You have forbidden us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with heavy deeds as You burdened those before us who were disobedient, as a punishment for them. Our Lord, and do not impose upon us what we cannot bear of duties and calamities. Blot out our sins, cover our faults, and be good to us. You are the Master of our affairs and the One who manages them. So grant us victory over those who denied Your religion, disbelieved in Your oneness, and called Your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) a liar, and make the final outcome ours over them in this world and the Hereafter."
